Heat 15ml olive oil in a pan over medium-high heat. Sear chicken breast for 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown and internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Remove chicken from pan. Rest for 5 minutes. Cut into small, irregular chunks.
Segment oranges and grapefruit. Remove all white pith.
Toast pistachios in a dry pan over medium heat for 3-4 minutes until fragrant. Roughly chop.
Prepare dressing: Whisk honey, lemon juice, Dijon mustard, and a pinch of salt and pepper in a small bowl.
Arrange roasted carrots, citrus segments, and chicken chunks artfully on 4 plates.
Drizzle dressing over the salad components.
Garnish with chopped pistachios and micro-cilantro.

recipes.recipe_name: Fudgy Chocolate Brownies
recipes.visual_description: A single generous square of fudgy chocolate brownie rests on a simple, well-loved ceramic dessert plate. The brownie has a deep, rich brown color with a slightly crackled, matte top surface. Its edges are clean, indicating a soft, dense interior. The texture appears moist and dense, characteristic of a fudgy brownie, with no visible dryness. A few small, natural crumbs might be scattered casually around the base of the brownie on the plate. The plate itself is off-white or cream-colored, with a slight rustic imperfection. It sits on a warm, worn wooden kitchen table. The lighting is soft and natural, suggesting a cozy, lived-in family kitchen environment. A simple, folded cloth napkin in a neutral tone is casually placed beside the plate. The scene is unpretentious, inviting, and focused on comfort.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve warm or at room temperature
Pair with a scoop of vanilla ice cream
Enjoy with a glass of milk or coffee
instructions: Preheat oven to 175°C. Line a 20x20 cm baking pan with parchment paper.
Melt chocolate and butter together in a heatproof bowl set over a pot of simmering water. Stir until smooth. Remove from heat.
In a separate large bowl, whisk granulated sugar and eggs until light and fluffy.
Stir vanilla extract into the egg mixture.
Gradually fold the melted chocolate mixture into the egg mixture until just combined. Do not overmix.
Sift flour and cocoa powder into the wet mixture. Add salt. Fold gently until no dry streaks remain.
Pour batter into the prepared baking pan. Spread evenly.
Bake for 25-30 minutes. A toothpick inserted into the center should come out with moist crumbs, not wet batter.
Cool completely in the pan on a wire rack before cutting into squares.

recipes.recipe_name: Dark Chocolate Crémeux, Hazelnut Sable, Raspberry Fluid Gel
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Dark Chocolate Crémeux, Hazelnut Sable, and Raspberry Fluid Gel is artfully arranged on a pristine white bone china plate. Abundant negative space highlights each element. The dark chocolate crémeux, a velvety, deep brown, forms a perfectly glossy quenelle, showcasing its smooth texture. Adjacent, a crisp, golden-brown hazelnut sable shard, irregularly broken, offers contrasting crumbly texture. A vibrant crimson raspberry fluid gel is delicately swiped across the plate, providing a bright, tart accent. Two fresh, ruby-red raspberries are precisely placed, their natural form complementing the refined composition. The dish rests on a premium white Carrara marble, illuminated by dramatic professional lighting, enhancing its sophisticated, minimalist elegance. A precisely folded white linen napkin completes the luxurious setting.
instructions: Prepare Hazelnut Sable:
Combine diced cold butter, icing sugar, almond flour, hazelnut flour, plain flour, and salt in a bowl. Rub butter into dry ingredients until crumbly.
Add the egg yolk. Mix briefly until a dough forms. Do not overmix.
Form the dough into a disc. Wrap in cling film. Chill for 30 minutes.
Preheat oven to 160°C.
Roll the chilled dough 3 mm thick between two sheets of parchment paper.
Cut into desired shapes, such as 5 cm squares or circles.
Bake for 12-15 minutes, or until golden brown. Cool completely on a wire rack.
Prepare Dark Chocolate Crémeux:
Finely chop the dark chocolate. Place it in a heatproof bowl.
In a separate bowl, whisk the 3 egg yolks and 30 g granulated sugar until pale and creamy.
Heat heavy cream and whole milk in a saucepan until simmering.
Slowly pour the hot cream mixture over the egg yolk mixture, whisking constantly.
Return the entire mixture to the saucepan. Cook over medium-low heat, stirring constantly with a spatula, until the mixture slightly thickens (nappe consistency, 82-84°C). Do not boil.
Pour the hot custard through a fine-mesh sieve directly over the chopped chocolate.
Let sit for 1 minute. Emulsify with an immersion blender or spatula until smooth and glossy.
Pour the crémeux into a shallow dish. Cover the surface directly with cling film to prevent a skin from forming.
Chill for a minimum of 4 hours, or preferably overnight, until firm.
Prepare Raspberry Fluid Gel:
Blend fresh raspberries, 20 g granulated sugar, and water until smooth.
Pass the mixture through a fine-mesh sieve to remove all seeds and pulp.
Transfer the strained liquid to a small saucepan. Whisk in the agar-agar powder.
Bring the mixture to a boil, whisking constantly. Boil for 1 minute.
Pour the hot gel into a shallow dish. Chill until set, approximately 30 minutes.
Once set, transfer the firm gel to a blender. Blend until completely smooth and fluid.
Pass the fluid gel through a fine-mesh sieve for ultimate smoothness.
Transfer the finished fluid gel to a squeeze bottle or piping bag. Keep chilled until plating.
Assembly and Plating:
Place one hazelnut sable piece slightly off-center on each serving plate.
Using a warmed spoon, form a perfect quenelle of the dark chocolate crémeux. Carefully place it next to the sable.
Artfully place a few dots or a delicate smear of the raspberry fluid gel around the crémeux and sable.
Arrange 2-3 fresh raspberries beside the crémeux for added color and freshness.
Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Potato Salad with Tangy Vinaigrette
recipes.visual_description: The potato salad is presented in an everyday ceramic serving bowl, generous and unpretentious. Diced waxy potatoes, coated in a glossy, tangy vinaigrette, form the base. Interspersed throughout are finely diced pieces of vibrant red onion, crisp green celery, and bright red bell pepper, adding contrasting colors and textures. Freshly chopped green parsley is sprinkled over the top, providing a pop of color and freshness. The salad is casually tossed, showcasing the varied components in a natural, organic arrangement. The bowl sits on a well-used wooden dining table. A simple, sturdy fork rests beside the bowl on a casually placed cloth napkin. Warm, inviting light from a kitchen fixture illuminates the scene, creating a cozy, lived-in atmosphere. The entire plate is visible, with adequate negative space around the bowl, highlighting the wholesome, comforting nature of the dish.
instructions: Wash potatoes. Peel if desired. Cut potatoes into 2 cm diced cubes.
Place diced potatoes in a large pot. Cover with cold water. Add a generous pinch of salt.
Bring water to a boil. Cook potatoes until fork-tender, about 10-15 minutes. Do not overcook.
Drain potatoes thoroughly in a colander. Let steam dry for a few minutes.
While potatoes cook, finely dice the red onion, celery stalks, and red bell pepper.
Chop fresh parsley.
In a small bowl, whisk together olive oil, apple cider vinegar, vegetable broth, Dijon mustard, and sugar. Season with salt and black pepper.
Place warm, drained potatoes into a large mixing bowl.
Pour the dressing over the warm potatoes. Gently toss to coat evenly. The warm potatoes will absorb the dressing.
Add the finely diced red onion, celery, and red bell pepper to the bowl. Add chopped parsley.
Gently fold all ingredients together until well combined.
Taste and adjust seasoning if needed. Serve warm or at room temperature.

recipes.recipe_name: Potato and Celery Salad
recipes.visual_description: The Potato and Celery Salad is presented in a large, rustic ceramic serving bowl on a well-used wooden dining table. The salad features evenly cut 2 cm potato cubes, coated in a creamy, pale yellow mayonnaise-based dressing. Interspersed throughout are bright green chopped celery, small flecks of purple-red diced red onion, and visible pieces of chopped hard-boiled egg, showing both white and yellow. Fresh green dill is scattered over the top as a garnish, adding a pop of color. The texture appears creamy and slightly chunky. The bowl is positioned slightly off-center. A simple, everyday ceramic plate with a fork rests beside the serving bowl, suggesting a casual, homely meal. Lighting is warm and cozy, as if from kitchen fixtures.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Served chilled as a side dish at barbecues, potlucks, and family gatherings.
Often accompanied by grilled meats or sandwiches.
instructions: Wash and peel potatoes. Cut potatoes into 2 cm cubes.
Place potato cubes in a large pot. Cover with cold water by 2 cm. Add a pinch of salt.
Bring water to a boil. Reduce heat and simmer until potatoes are tender, about 10-15 minutes. Do not overcook.
Drain potatoes thoroughly. Let them cool slightly in the colander for 5 minutes to release steam.
In a large bowl, combine mayonnaise, Dijon mustard, white wine vinegar, salt, and black pepper. Whisk until smooth.
Add cooled potatoes, chopped celery, diced red onion, chopped hard-boiled eggs, and chopped fresh dill to the bowl with the dressing.
Gently fold all ingredients together until well combined. Be careful not to mash potatoes.
Taste and adjust seasoning if needed.
Cover and chill salad in the refrigerator for at least 1 hour before serving.
notes: For best flavor, make the salad a few hours ahead to allow flavors to meld.
Do not overcook potatoes; they should be tender but still hold their shape.

recipes.recipe_name: Poulet à la Moutarde
recipes.visual_description: A single, whole pan-seared chicken thigh with crisp, golden-brown skin sits centrally on a clean white porcelain plate. To the side, four precise 5cm carrot batons are neatly stacked, glistening with a clear butter glaze. A rich, glossy cream sauce, speckled with dark whole grain mustard seeds and bright green tarragon bits, is elegantly draped over the chicken, flowing slightly onto the plate surface. The arrangement is clean with ample negative space. The setting is a modern French bistro with a light oak table. A white cotton napkin and polished silver cutlery rest beside the plate. Natural, soft daylight from the side enhances the textures of the poultry skin and the velvety sauce.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty baguette to soak up the mustard sauce
Pair with a dry white wine such as Chardonnay or Aligoté
Follow with a simple green salad with vinaigrette
instructions: Season chicken thighs generously with salt and pepper.
Heat oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Place chicken skin-side down in the pan.
Sear for 6 minutes until the skin is golden and crisp.
Flip the chicken and cook for 2 minutes.
Transfer chicken to a plate and set aside.
Lower heat to medium and add 30g butter to the pan.
Add diced onions and sauté for 5 minutes until soft.
Pour in chicken stock and deglaze the pan by scraping the bottom.
Whisk in Dijon and whole grain mustards until smooth.
Return chicken to the skillet, skin-side up.
Simmer for 10-12 minutes until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C.
Steam or boil carrot batons in salted water for 5 minutes until tender.
Drain carrots and toss with remaining 10g butter.
Remove chicken from the skillet and whisk heavy cream into the sauce.
Simmer sauce for 3 minutes until thickened.
Stir in fresh tarragon.
Serve one whole chicken thigh per plate with carrots and sauce.
notes: Do not cover the pan while simmering to keep the chicken skin crisp
Ensure the sauce does not boil vigorously after adding cream to prevent splitting
Always use a meat thermometer to confirm the 75°C internal temperature

recipes.recipe_name: Confit Chicken Thigh with Fermented Garlic Honey & Pickled Radish
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a handcrafted, matte cream-beige ceramic plate with a natural, slightly textured finish, placed on a light, reclaimed wooden table. A single, tender confit chicken thigh, still retaining its natural shape, sits off-center on the white space of the plate. Its rich, golden-brown hue from the confit process contrasts gently with the plate. Beside the chicken, a neat, small mound of thinly sliced, vibrant pink and white pickled radish rounds creates a fresh, bright accent. A generous, glossy drizzle of amber-colored fermented garlic honey cascades over the chicken, catching the soft natural light. A few irregular, crisp shards of golden-brown chicken skin are artfully placed near the chicken, providing textural contrast. A delicate sprinkle of finely chopped fresh chives adds a touch of subtle green. The composition is clean, minimalistic, and unforced, emphasizing the pure beauty and natural textures of each ingredient. The negative space on the plate is significant, drawing focus to the perfectly prepared elements. The background features a blurred hint of natural greenery and an undyed linen napkin in a natural beige tone, maintaining an eco-conscious, earthy aesthetic.
instructions: Prepare Fermented Garlic Honey (at least 1 week in advance): Peel garlic cloves. Crush lightly. Combine garlic and honey in a clean, sterile jar. Seal jar loosely or use an airlock. Store at room temperature (18-24°C). Burp jar daily for the first week to release gas. Ferment for 1-4 weeks, or until garlic softens and honey thins.

Prepare Chicken Thighs for Confit: Pat chicken thighs very dry with paper towels. In a small bowl, combine 20g sea salt, 5g black peppercorns, and leaves from 2 thyme sprigs. Rub salt mixture generously over chicken thighs. Place chicken in a shallow dish, cover, and refrigerate for 8-12 hours. Rinse chicken thighs thoroughly under cold water to remove excess salt. Pat very dry.

Cook Chicken Confit: Preheat oven to 150°C (300°F). In a heavy-bottomed oven-safe pot or Dutch oven, melt duck or chicken fat over low heat. Add rinsed and dried chicken thighs, ensuring they are fully submerged in the fat. Add bay leaves and remaining 2 thyme sprigs. Cover pot and transfer to preheated oven. Cook for 2.5-3 hours, or until chicken is very tender and meat easily pulls from bone. Carefully remove chicken from fat. Strain fat and reserve for future use. Let chicken cool slightly. Remove bones and discard. Keep skin intact.

Prepare Pickled Radishes: Wash radishes. Slice thinly into rounds or half-moons. In a small saucepan, combine white wine vinegar, water, 15g sugar, and 5g sea salt. Bring to a simmer, stirring until sugar and salt dissolve. Place sliced radishes in a clean jar or heatproof bowl. Pour hot pickling brine over radishes. Let cool to room temperature. Refrigerate for at least 30 minutes before serving.

Crisp Chicken Skin: Preheat oven to 200°C (390°F) or a non-stick pan over medium-high heat. Place chicken skin, fat-side down, on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper or in the hot pan. Bake for 10-15 minutes, or pan-fry until golden brown and very crispy. Remove and drain on paper towels. Break into irregular shards.

Finish and Plate: Gently reheat confit chicken thigh meat (without skin) in a small amount of confit fat or in a warm oven until heated through (internal temperature 75°C / 167°F). Place one reheated confit chicken thigh on each serving plate. Arrange a small mound of pickled radish slices beside the chicken. Drizzle generously with fermented garlic honey. Garnish with a few shards of crispy chicken skin and a sprinkle of chopped fresh chives. Serve immediately.
notes: Fermented garlic honey requires at least one week of fermentation time before use.

recipes.recipe_name: Spanish Tortilla with Chorizo and Piquillo Peppers
recipes.visual_description: A thick, golden-brown Spanish Tortilla wedge sits centrally on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The tortilla's exterior is subtly crisp, revealing a tender, cohesive interior packed with soft potato slices, translucent onion, vibrant red piquillo pepper strips, and rich orange-red chorizo chunks. A generous dollop of creamy, pale yellow garlic aioli rests beside the tortilla, with a small sprig of fresh parsley for a touch of green. The plate is positioned on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by a folded cotton napkin and traditional flatware. Natural, even lighting highlights the varied textures and warm color palette. The scene is uncluttered, showcasing a single, hearty portion.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread for dipping in aioli.
Offer a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and vinegar.
Enjoy with a glass of dry Spanish cider or red wine.
instructions: Heat 300 ml olive oil in a 24 cm non-stick pan over medium-low heat. Add peeled and thinly sliced potatoes (2-3 mm) and thinly sliced onion. Cook gently for 20-25 minutes until very tender but not browned. Drain potatoes and onions in a colander, reserving oil. Season with salt and pepper.
While potatoes cook, sauté 5 mm rounds of chorizo in a separate pan over medium heat until crispy. Drain excess fat.
In a large bowl, whisk eggs thoroughly. Stir in cooked potatoes, onions, chorizo, and sliced piquillo pepper strips. Let stand 5 minutes for flavors to meld.
Heat a clean 24 cm non-stick pan with 15 ml fresh olive oil over medium heat. Pour in egg mixture. Cook for 5-7 minutes until edges are set and bottom is golden.
Place a large plate over the pan. Invert the tortilla onto the plate. Slide the tortilla back into the pan, uncooked side down. Cook for another 3-5 minutes until fully set and golden.
For Aioli: In a small bowl, whisk egg yolk and minced garlic. Slowly drizzle in extra virgin olive oil while continuously whisking until emulsified and thick. Stir in lemon juice and salt.
Slice tortilla into wedges. Serve warm or at room temperature with a dollop of aioli.
notes: The reserved olive oil from cooking potatoes can be reused for other dishes.
traditional_techniques: Slow frying potatoes in olive oil for tenderness
Preparing a traditional emulsion for aioli

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken Supreme, Verjus-Mustard Jus, Saffron Potato Purée
recipes.visual_description: A single pan-seared chicken supreme, presented whole with its golden-crisp skin facing upwards, rests precisely atop a creamy, pale yellow saffron potato purée. The purée is artfully swept across the pristine white, circular designer plate, leaving abundant negative space. A glossy, amber verjus-mustard jus is elegantly spooned around the chicken, creating an inviting pool. Delicate strands of golden-brown crispy leek are delicately piled on the chicken, adding a textural contrast and subtle height. A few vibrant green chervil sprigs or microgreens provide a fresh, precise accent. The setting features a premium grey-veined marble surface, a pristine white linen napkin folded into a precise triangle, and elegant, modern cutlery. Dramatic professional lighting casts soft, intentional shadows, highlighting the dish's refined textures and sophisticated color palette. The background is ultra-minimalist, ensuring the dish remains the sole focal point.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C. Pat chicken supremes dry with paper towels. Season generously with salt and pepper.
For the saffron potato purée: Peel and dice potatoes into 2cm cubes. Place in a saucepan, cover with cold salted water. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer until very tender (15-20 minutes).
While potatoes cook, gently warm milk and saffron in a small saucepan. Do not boil.
Drain potatoes thoroughly. Pass through a ricer or mash well. Gradually whisk in warm saffron milk and 50g butter until smooth and creamy. Season with salt. Keep warm.

For the crispy leek: Thinly slice the white part of the leek into fine julienne strips. Heat a small amount of olive oil in a pan over medium-high heat. Fry leek until golden and crispy. Drain on paper towels. Season lightly with salt.

For the chicken: Heat remaining olive oil in an oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Place chicken supremes skin-side down. Sear for 8-10 minutes until skin is deeply golden and crispy. Do not move chicken during this time.
Flip chicken supremes. Transfer skillet to the preheated oven. Roast for 10-15 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Remove chicken from oven. Transfer to a cutting board. Rest for 5 minutes, tented loosely with foil.
For the verjus-mustard jus: Discard excess fat from the skillet, leaving about 15ml. Add minced shallots to the skillet. Sauté over medium heat until softened (2-3 minutes).
Deglaze skillet with verjus. Scrape up any browned bits. Reduce by half.
Pour in chicken stock. Bring to a simmer and reduce by one-third. Whisk in Dijon mustard.
Remove skillet from heat. Whisk in remaining 30g cold butter, one piece at a time, until jus is glossy and emulsified. Season with salt and pepper.

To plate: Spoon a generous dollop or sweep of saffron potato purée onto the center of each plate. Place one chicken supreme on top of the purée. Artfully spoon the verjus-mustard jus around the chicken. Garnish with a small pile of crispy leek on the chicken and a sprig of fresh chervil or microgreens.

recipes.recipe_name: Mediterranean Stuffed Mushrooms with Olive-Feta Rice
recipes.visual_description: Four large Mediterranean stuffed mushrooms are arranged naturally on a handcrafted cream-beige ceramic plate, showcasing an organic, slightly asymmetrical composition. Each mushroom cap is a rich earthy brown, generously filled with a vibrant mixture of white rice, dark chopped Kalamata olives, creamy crumbled feta, and bright green chopped parsley. The filling has a slight golden hue from baking and a sheen from olive oil. Diced mushroom stems are integrated, demonstrating zero-waste. Fresh parsley leaves and a lemon wedge provide natural garnish and color. The plate rests on a light, textured reclaimed wood surface, with an undyed linen napkin visible. Soft, natural light illuminates the scene. The background is clean, minimalist, with a subtle green plant enhancing the eco-conscious aesthetic.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve warm or at room temperature as part of a shared mezze or antipasti platter.
Accompany with crusty bread for dipping in any residual juices.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C. Line a baking tray.
Clean mushrooms. Gently remove stems. Dice mushroom stems finely.
Heat olive oil in a pan over medium heat. Add diced onion and mushroom stems. Sauté 5-7 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic. Sauté 1 minute until fragrant.
Remove pan from heat. In a bowl, combine sautéed mixture with cooked rice, chopped olives, crumbled feta, chopped parsley, and lemon zest. Mix well.
Season filling with salt and black pepper. Taste and adjust.
Place mushroom caps on the baking tray. Generously spoon filling into each mushroom cap.
Drizzle stuffed mushrooms with extra olive oil.
Bake 20-25 minutes, or until mushrooms are tender and filling is heated through and lightly golden.
Squeeze fresh lemon juice over baked mushrooms before serving.
notes: This recipe utilizes mushroom stems and leftover rice for a zero-waste approach.
Adjust seasoning to your preference. A pinch of red pepper flakes can add a subtle kick.

recipes.recipe_name: Shepherd's Pie
recipes.visual_description: A deep, oval ceramic baking dish, filled with golden-brown Shepherd's Pie. The mashed potato topping is textured with fork tines, some peaks are slightly crisped and golden. Visible patches of the rich, dark meat and vegetable filling peek through the sides. Diced carrots and peas are discernible within the savory lamb mincemeat gravy. The overall impression is hearty and comforting. A single, generous portion is scooped directly from the baking dish onto a simple, round ceramic plate with a slight rim. The edges of the potato crust are slightly uneven, indicating a home-cooked feel. The plate rests on a well-used, warm-toned wooden dining table. A simple, folded off-white linen napkin is casually placed to the side. A basic fork is next to the plate. Lighting is warm and inviting, typical of a cozy kitchen.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a simple green salad on the side
Serve with crusty bread for soaking up any extra gravy
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C. Peel potatoes. Cut into large chunks. Place in a large pot. Cover with cold salted water. Bring to a boil. Cook until very tender, about 15-20 minutes.

While potatoes cook, heat vegetable oil in a large oven-safe casserole dish or deep frying pan over medium-high heat. Add lamb mincemeat. Brown thoroughly, breaking up clumps. Cook until no pink remains. Drain excess fat.
Add diced onion and diced carrots to the pan with the mincemeat. Cook, stirring occasionally, for 5-7 minutes until softened. Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.

Stir in plain flour. Cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly. Add tomato paste, Worcestershire sauce, and stock. Stir well. Bring mixture to a simmer. Reduce heat to low. Cook for 10-15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until sauce thickens.
Stir in frozen peas. Season the meat mixture with salt and black pepper.
Drain cooked potatoes. Return to the pot. Add butter and milk. Mash until smooth. Season mashed potatoes with salt and black pepper.
Spoon the meat mixture evenly into the oven-safe dish. Top with mashed potatoes. Spread evenly with a spoon or spatula. Create peaks and ridges on the potato topping using a fork.
Bake for 25-30 minutes, or until the potato topping is golden brown and the filling is bubbling. Let stand for 5 minutes before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken Rillette with Fermented Garlic & Sourdough
recipes.visual_description: A single starter portion of Chicken Rillette is elegantly presented on a handcrafted ceramic plate in a natural cream or beige tone. The plate rests on a light bamboo or reclaimed wood table surface. A thick, irregular slice of golden-brown sourdough toast serves as the base. A rustic mound of light golden-brown chicken rillette, showcasing its shredded texture, is spooned onto the toast. A few soft, amber-colored fermented garlic cloves are nestled on top of the rillette, adding visual interest. A small, vibrant cluster of quick-pickled seasonal vegetables, such as thinly sliced pink radish and translucent orange carrot, is artfully arranged beside the rillette, providing a fresh contrast in color and texture. A tiny sprig of fresh thyme or a few microgreens provide a subtle green accent. The composition is minimalistic, emphasizing clean lines and natural textures. Ample negative space surrounds the dish, highlighting its pure beauty. An undyed linen napkin in natural beige is folded neatly beside the plate. The scene is illuminated by soft, natural lighting, creating a clean, inviting aesthetic with a minimalist background that may include subtle natural elements or plants.
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and black pepper.
In a heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven, render chicken skin over medium heat until crispy. Remove crispy skin. Reserve for garnish or discard. Keep rendered fat in pot.
Sear chicken thighs in rendered fat until golden brown on all sides. Remove chicken from pot.
Add fermented garlic cloves to the pot. Sauté gently for 1 minute until fragrant.
Return chicken thighs to the pot. Add bay leaf, thyme sprigs, and chicken stock.
Bring liquid to a gentle simmer. Cover the pot. Reduce heat to low. Cook for 1.5 to 2 hours, or until chicken is extremely tender and easily falls off the bone.
Carefully remove chicken from the pot. Discard bones and bay leaf. Shred chicken meat using two forks. Set aside.
Increase heat under the pot. Reduce cooking liquid until slightly thickened, about 5-7 minutes. Remove thyme sprigs.

Combine shredded chicken with reduced cooking liquid and a portion of the reserved rendered chicken fat (start with 2-3 tablespoons, add more if needed) in a bowl. Mix until moist and spreadable. Adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
Toast sourdough slices until golden and crisp.
Spoon chicken rillette generously onto each toasted sourdough slice. Top with a few extra fermented garlic cloves.

recipes.recipe_name: Beef & Bone Marrow Boudin Blanc, Parsnip Purée, Red Wine Jus
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of an ultra-sophisticated main course is presented on a pristine, large white bone china plate, allowing for abundant negative space. Two to three perfectly seared, golden-brown beef and bone marrow boudin blanc medallions are positioned naturally. Adjacent to them, a velvety, pale ivory parsnip purée is artfully swooshed or dolloped. A rich, glossy ruby-red red wine jus is meticulously drizzled around the components, creating elegant lines. The dish is subtly garnished with a sparse scattering of vibrant, finely minced chives. The textures are varied: a delicate crust on the boudin contrasting with its smooth interior, a silken purée, and a viscous jus. The color palette is refined with golden browns, creamy whites, deep reds, and hints of green. The plate rests on a premium grey-veined marble surface, illuminated by dramatic, professional lighting that casts subtle shadows, enhancing depth. A precisely folded white linen napkin and elegant, minimalist flatware complete the luxurious, uncluttered Michelin-starred setting.

ingredients.name: Roasted beef bones or high-quality beef stock

instructions: Prepare Red Wine Jus: Roast beef bones until deeply browned. Transfer to a pot. Add sliced shallot, crushed garlic, thyme, bay leaf, peppercorns. Deglaze roasting pan with red wine; add to pot. Cover with water or beef stock. Simmer gently for 4-6 hours, skimming impurities. Strain liquid through a fine-mesh sieve. Reduce strained liquid over medium heat until syrupy and concentrated. Season with salt. Finish with a knob of butter before serving for gloss.

Prepare Parsnip Purée: Peel parsnips. Cut into 2 cm chunks. Place in a saucepan, cover with milk and water (50/50). Add a pinch of salt. Bring to a boil, then simmer until very tender. Drain liquid, reserving a little. Transfer parsnips to a high-speed blender with 20g butter. Blend until perfectly smooth and creamy. Add a splash of reserved cooking liquid if needed. Pass purée through a fine-mesh chinois for ultimate smoothness. Season with salt.

Prepare Beef & Bone Marrow Boudin Blanc: Score bone marrow. Poach gently in simmering water for 2-3 minutes until softened. Scoop out marrow; chill. Finely dice 1 shallot. Sauté in 10g butter until translucent. Deglaze with Cognac; reduce completely. Cool. In a food processor, combine beef mincemeat, chilled bone marrow, sautéed shallot, egg white, heavy cream, salt, white pepper, and nutmeg. Process until a very smooth, emulsified paste forms. Do not overmix to avoid toughness.

Form and Cook Boudin Blanc: Lay out plastic wrap. Spoon the boudin mixture onto the plastic wrap. Form into four uniform logs, approximately 3 cm in diameter and 10 cm long. Roll tightly, twisting ends to create compact cylinders. Poach boudin logs gently in simmering water (not boiling) for 15-20 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 65°C. Transfer to an ice bath to chill completely. Remove plastic wrap.

Sear and Serve: Heat remaining butter in a non-stick pan over medium-high heat. Slice chilled boudin logs into 2-3 thick medallions each. Sear medallions for 2-3 minutes per side until golden brown and a slight crust forms. Reheat parsnip purée and red wine jus gently.

Plate: Create a swoosh or artistic dollop of parsnip purée on one side of a pristine white plate. Place 2-3 seared boudin medallions artfully next to the purée. Drizzle a generous amount of the rich red wine jus around the elements. Garnish minimally with finely minced chives.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken Breast with Parsnip Puree and Thyme Jus
recipes.visual_description: A single, elegant portion of pan-seared chicken breast is the focal point on a pristine, subtly patterned bone china plate. The chicken, with its crispy, golden-brown skin, is placed whole, allowing its natural form to shine. Beside it, a smooth, creamy parsnip puree forms a delicate, organic swoosh, its off-white hue contrasting subtly with the chicken. A rich, glossy thyme jus is artfully drizzled around the main components, creating fluid, dark brown accents on the white plate. A tiny, vibrant green fresh thyme sprig garnishes the dish precisely. The arrangement features abundant negative space. The plate rests on a premium white Carrara marble surface, accompanied by a precisely folded white linen napkin. Dramatic professional lighting casts soft shadows, enhancing the refined, minimalist presentation.
instructions: Prepare Parsnip Puree: Peel parsnips. Cut into 2cm rounds. Place in a saucepan. Cover with cold salted water. Bring to a boil. Reduce heat. Simmer until very tender, about 15-20 minutes. Drain well. Return parsnips to the pan. Add 30g butter and cream. Mash until smooth. Season with salt and pepper. Keep warm.

Prepare Thyme Jus: Finely chop shallot. In a small saucepan, heat 10ml olive oil. Add shallot. Sauté until softened, about 2 minutes. Add chicken stock and 2 thyme sprigs. Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat. Simmer gently until reduced by half and slightly thickened, about 15-20 minutes. Strain through a fine-mesh sieve. Discard solids. Season with salt and pepper. Keep warm.

Cook Chicken: Pat chicken breasts dry. Season skin and flesh generously with salt and pepper. Heat remaining 20ml olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Place chicken skin-side down in the hot skillet. Sear for 6-8 minutes until skin is deeply golden brown and crispy. Flip chicken. Add remaining 20g butter and 2 fresh thyme sprigs to the skillet. Baste chicken with melted butter. Transfer skillet to a preheated oven at 180°C (350°F). Roast for 10-12 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Remove from oven. Rest chicken on a cutting board for 5 minutes.

Plate: Spoon a generous quenelle or swoosh of parsnip puree onto the center of each plate. Place one whole, rested pan-seared chicken breast beside the puree. Drizzle the thyme jus artfully around the chicken and puree. Garnish with a small fresh thyme sprig.

recipes.recipe_name: Poached Chicken Quenelles with Saffron Nage and English Pea Coulis
recipes.visual_description: A single, refined serving is presented on a wide-rimmed, matte off-white bone china plate. Two perfectly smooth, pale ivory poached chicken quenelles, shaped like elongated ovals, rest delicately in a shallow pool of clear, golden saffron nage. The quenelles appear light and cloud-like, with a soft, uniform texture. Adjacent to the quenelles, a small, precise dot of vibrant green English pea coulis adds a pop of contrasting color. A single, delicate chervil sprig is placed artfully on one quenelle. The composition emphasizes abundant negative space, highlighting the precision and purity of each element. The plate is positioned on a polished dark wood surface, complemented by a pristine white linen napkin folded into a precise triangle. Dramatic, directional lighting casts soft shadows, enhancing the dish's sculptural quality. The background is ultra-minimalist, drawing full attention to the sophisticated culinary creation.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with traditional French cutlery
instructions: Chill chicken mincemeat, cream, and egg white thoroughly. Combine chicken mincemeat, chilled cream, and egg white in a food processor. Process until very smooth and emulsified. Season with salt and white pepper. Pass mixture through a fine-mesh sieve for ultimate smoothness. Chill for 30 minutes.

For the saffron nage, melt 20g butter in a saucepan. Add minced shallots and cook until translucent. Deglaze with white wine. Reduce by half. Add chicken stock and saffron threads. Simmer gently for 15 minutes. Strain the nage through a fine-mesh sieve. Keep warm.

For the pea coulis, blanch English peas in boiling salted water for 2 minutes. Immediately transfer to an ice bath to stop cooking and preserve color. Drain well. Blend peas with fresh mint leaves and 30ml of the saffron nage until very smooth. Pass through a fine-mesh sieve. Season with salt. Keep warm.

Bring a large pot of lightly salted water to a gentle simmer. Using two large spoons, form oval-shaped quenelles from the chicken mixture. Gently slide quenelles into simmering water. Poach for 8-10 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Remove quenelles with a slotted spoon. Drain well.

To plate, spoon a small pool of saffron nage onto the center of each plate. Place two poached chicken quenelles artfully in the nage. Create a small, precise dot or swipe of pea coulis beside the quenelles. Garnish with a single delicate chervil sprig. Serve immediately.
notes: Ensure all chicken mixture ingredients are very cold for best emulsification and texture.
Do not boil the quenelles; maintain a gentle simmer to prevent breaking and ensure even cooking.

recipes.recipe_name: Mushroom and Feta Rice Pilaf
recipes.visual_description: A single, modest portion of Mushroom and Feta Rice Pilaf is casually mounded on an everyday, off-white ceramic plate with subtle imperfections. The pilaf features fluffy white rice, interspersed with tender, earthy sliced mushrooms and glistening whole Kalamata olives. Crumbs of creamy white feta cheese are generously scattered over the top, melting slightly into the warm rice. Fresh, vibrant green chopped parsley is sprinkled over the dish, adding a pop of color and freshness. The arrangement is natural and organic, with components touching and overlapping slightly, reflecting a comforting home-cooked meal. The plate rests on a well-used wooden dining table. A simple metal fork and a casually folded linen napkin are placed beside the plate. Warm, soft lighting from kitchen fixtures illuminates the scene, creating a cozy, lived-in atmosphere typical of a family kitchen.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread for dipping.
Accompany with a simple Greek salad.
Serve family-style from a large communal bowl.
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large skillet or pot over medium heat.
Add diced onion. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add sliced mushrooms. Cook until tender and browned, about 8-10 minutes.
Stir in minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add rice to the skillet. Stir to coat rice grains with oil and mushroom juices. Toast for 2 minutes.
Pour in vegetable broth. Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to low, cover, and cook for 15-20 minutes. Or until rice is tender and liquid is absorbed. If needed, add a splash of water.
Remove from heat. Stir in pitted Kalamata olives, crumbled feta cheese, lemon zest, lemon juice, and chopped fresh parsley.
Fluff the pilaf gently with a fork.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste. Serve warm.
notes: Adjust broth quantity based on rice type for desired consistency.
Taste and adjust seasoning before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Mexican Chicken and Rice Bowl with Roasted Corn & Tomato Salsa
recipes.visual_description: A vibrant Mexican Chicken and Rice Bowl is presented in a wide, shallow, off-white ceramic bowl, centered on a light wooden table. The base is a fluffy mound of white long-grain rice. Generous, golden-brown seared chicken chunks are nestled on one side of the rice. Adjacent to the chicken, a colorful roasted corn and cherry tomato salsa, with slightly charred corn kernels and burst tomatoes, creates a textural contrast. Black beans and bright green peas are distinctively placed on the other side, adding depth and color. A generous drizzle of creamy lime-cilantro crema elegantly zigzags over the chicken and salsa. Fresh cilantro leaves are scattered as a garnish, and a lime wedge sits on the rim of the bowl. The overall composition is balanced, showcasing distinct ingredients with natural, organic placement. A simple linen napkin and a fork are positioned beside the bowl, with soft, natural light illuminating the dish.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm corn or flour tortillas on the side
Offer extra lime wedges for squeezing
instructions: Rinse rice under cold water. Combine rice and 500ml water in a pot. Bring to boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes. Remove from heat, let stand 5 minutes, then fluff with a fork.

Preheat oven to 200°C. On a baking sheet, toss halved cherry tomatoes and corn kernels with 15ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Roast for 15-20 minutes, until corn is slightly charred and tomatoes are tender.

Heat remaining 15ml olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Cut chicken into 3cm chunks. Season chicken chunks with salt, pepper, chili powder, cumin, and smoked paprika. Add chicken to skillet. Sear chicken until golden brown on all sides and cooked through, about 8-10 minutes. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Add diced onion and minced garlic to the skillet with the chicken. Cook for 3-4 minutes until softened.
Add rinsed black beans, green peas, and chicken broth to the skillet. Bring to a simmer. Cook for 5 minutes until heated through and liquid slightly reduces.
In a small bowl, combine mayonnaise, juice and zest from the lime, and chopped cilantro. Stir well to make the crema.
Divide cooked rice among 4 bowls. Top rice with chicken and bean mixture. Spoon roasted corn and tomato salsa over the dish. Drizzle generously with lime-cilantro crema. Garnish with fresh cilantro.
notes: Adjust chili powder to desired spice level
Fresh corn can be cut from the cob or use good quality frozen corn

recipes.recipe_name: Braised Beef & Mushroom Bites with Pickled Vegetables
recipes.visual_description: An elegant serving platter of natural stone or reclaimed wood holds 8-12 perfectly spaced canapés. Each bite begins with a delicate, pale green celery crisp, thinly sliced into small rounds or short batons, showcasing its natural texture. Topped centrally is a rich, dark brown mound of finely shredded, slow-braised beef, intermingled with diced sautéed mushrooms. The beef is tender, yet holds its form, creating an inviting, savory focal point. A small cluster of vibrant, julienned pickled carrots and translucent, pale pink pickled onions adds a bright pop of color and a contrasting tangy crunch. A scattering of finely chopped fresh parsley or chives provides a final verdant touch. The presentation is clean and minimalistic, allowing each ingredient's natural beauty to shine. The platter rests on a light bamboo table surface, complemented by an undyed linen napkin and soft natural light, with a clean, unobtrusive background.
instructions: For pickled vegetables: Julienne half onion and one carrot into thin strips. In a small saucepan, combine vinegar, sugar, 100ml water, and a pinch of salt. Bring to a simmer, stirring until sugar dissolves. Pour hot brine over julienned vegetables in a heatproof jar. Let cool completely, then refrigerate for at least 1 hour.
For braised beef: Dice remaining half onion, one carrot, and one celery stalk into 1cm pieces. Cut beef chuck into 2cm cubes. Season beef cubes generously with salt and pepper.
Heat 1 tablespoon olive oil in a heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high heat. Sear beef cubes in batches until deeply browned on all sides. Remove beef and set aside.
Add remaining 1 tablespoon olive oil to the pot. Add diced onion, carrot, and celery. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until softened. Add minced garlic, cook for 1 minute until fragrant.

Return seared beef to the pot. Pour in red wine and scrape up any browned bits from the bottom. Add beef broth, thyme sprigs, and bay leaf. Bring to a gentle simmer. Cover the pot, reduce heat to low, and braise for 2.5 to 3 hours, or until beef is fork-tender.

Remove beef from the pot. Shred finely using two forks. Strain the braising liquid through a fine-mesh sieve, discarding solids. Return strained liquid to the pot and reduce over medium-high heat until about 100ml of concentrated sauce remains. This may take 10-15 minutes.
Dice mixed mushrooms into small pieces. In a separate pan, sauté mushrooms in a little olive oil over medium-high heat until browned and tender. Season with salt and pepper.
Combine shredded beef, sautéed mushrooms, and reduced braising liquid. Mix well. Taste and adjust seasoning.

For celery crisps: Thinly slice the remaining celery stalk crosswise into small rounds or short batons. Toss with a drizzle of olive oil and a pinch of salt. Arrange in a single layer on a baking sheet. Bake at 180°C (350°F) for 10-15 minutes, or until crisp and lightly golden. Watch carefully to prevent burning.

To assemble canapés: Place a celery crisp on a serving platter. Top with a small spoonful of the braised beef and mushroom mixture. Garnish with a few strands of pickled carrot and onion. Finish with a sprinkle of finely chopped fresh parsley or chives. Serve immediately.
notes: This recipe emphasizes sustainable practices by utilizing tougher cuts of beef for braising, incorporating quick-pickled vegetables for preservation, and creating a zero-waste base from celery stalks. Prioritize locally sourced ingredients.

recipes.recipe_name: Mushroom, Feta, and Olive Rice Fritters
recipes.visual_description: Golden-brown, pan-fried rice fritters are casually arranged on an off-white, slightly chipped ceramic plate. Four to five roughly circular fritters, approximately 5-6 cm in diameter, are grouped together, some slightly overlapping, creating a natural, unpretentious cluster. A few chopped fresh parsley leaves are lightly sprinkled over the fritters for a touch of green. A half lemon wedge sits casually beside the fritters. The fritters' crispy exterior reveals visible bits of diced mushroom, crumbled white feta cheese, and dark chopped olive pieces within. The plate rests on a well-worn, light-colored wooden dining table. A simple, folded blue and white checkered cloth napkin is casually placed to one side. Warm, soft lighting, as if from an overhead kitchen fixture, casts gentle shadows, highlighting the fritters' inviting texture. The background is a soft blur of a homely kitchen, hinting at a lived-in atmosphere without distracting from the food.
instructions: Cook rice according to package directions. Let cool completely.
Clean mushrooms. Dice mushrooms into small cubes.
Heat 15ml olive oil in a pan over medium heat. Sauté diced mushrooms until tender and lightly browned. Remove from heat and cool.
Chop pitted olives finely.
Chop parsley finely.
In a large bowl, combine cooled cooked rice, sautéed mushrooms, chopped olives, crumbled feta cheese, chopped parsley, egg, and flour. Mix thoroughly until well combined.
Season the mixture with salt and pepper. Add the zest from half of the lemon.
Form the mixture into 12-16 small, flat fritters, approximately 5-6 cm in diameter and 1-1.5 cm thick.
Heat 30ml olive oil in a large non-stick pan over medium heat.
Cook fritters in batches for 3-4 minutes per side, until golden brown and crispy. Add more olive oil if needed for subsequent batches.
Squeeze fresh lemon juice from the remaining half lemon over the cooked fritters just before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Belgian Beer-Braised Chicken
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Belgian Beer-Braised Chicken is presented in a deep, clean white porcelain bowl. Two whole, tender chicken pieces (thigh and drumstick) are nestled in a rich, dark brown sauce. The sauce coats the chicken, revealing caramelized sliced onions and crispy diced bacon lardons. A few fresh thyme leaves are scattered over the dish for a vibrant green contrast. The textures are soft, succulent chicken and tender, sweet onions within a glossy, thick sauce. The plating is organized and balanced, leaving moderate negative space around the edges of the bowl. The setting is a modern bistro, with a simple light wooden table surface and a white linen napkin beside the bowl. Natural, even light illuminates the dish. A traditional Belgian beer glass is subtly visible in the soft-focus background, alongside a crust of rustic bread.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with Belgian frites (fries) or mashed potatoes.
Offer crusty bread to soak up the rich sauce.

ingredients.name: Chicken thighs and drumsticks, bone-in, skin-on

instructions: Pat chicken dry. Season with salt and pepper. Lightly dredge chicken pieces in flour. Shake off excess.
Heat vegetable oil in a large heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Add bacon lardons. Cook until crispy. Remove bacon with a slotted spoon. Set aside. Leave rendered fat in pot.
Add floured chicken pieces to the pot. Sear until golden brown on all sides. Do not overcrowd. Sear in batches if necessary. Remove chicken. Set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add sliced onions to the pot. Cook until softened and caramelized, about 8-10 minutes. Stir in minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Deglaze the pot with Belgian dark ale, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom.
Stir in beef stock, Dijon mustard, and brown sugar. Bring to a simmer.
Return chicken and cooked bacon lardons to the pot. Add thyme sprigs and bay leaf. Ensure chicken is mostly submerged.
Cover the pot. Reduce heat to low. Simmer for 45-60 minutes, or until chicken is very tender and cooked to an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).
Remove bay leaf and thyme sprigs. Adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
Serve hot, garnished with fresh chopped parsley.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
Use a good quality Belgian dark ale for authentic flavor.

recipes.recipe_name: Spicy Pork and Potato Croquettes
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a rustic light wooden serving board, showcasing a collection of golden-brown, elongated croquettes. Each croquette is uniformly shaped, approximately 6-7 cm long, with a visibly crispy, textured panko breadcrumb crust. A subtle fleck of red chili is occasionally visible through the golden exterior, hinting at the savory spice within. The croquettes are arranged organically, piled slightly, creating an inviting, abundant look. Beside the main pile, a small, clean white porcelain ramekin holds a vibrant chili-lime aioli, offering a creamy counterpoint. A light scattering of finely chopped fresh green chives is sprinkled over the croquettes, adding a pop of color and freshness. The background is a soft, blurred modern bistro setting, with hints of warm, natural lighting. The entire arrangement is clean and uncluttered, emphasizing the appetizing texture and color of the croquettes. The croquettes appear substantial and perfectly cooked, ready for sharing.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of chili-lime aioli for dipping.
instructions: Boil potatoes until tender. Drain well. Mash thoroughly. Season with salt and pepper. Set aside.
In a pan, melt butter over medium heat. Add diced onion and cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and diced chilies. Cook for 2 minutes until fragrant.
Pour in pork stock. Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat and cook until liquid is reduced by half and slightly thickened.
Combine the reduced stock mixture with the mashed potatoes. Mix well until fully incorporated. Taste and adjust seasoning.
Allow potato mixture to cool completely. Chill in the refrigerator for at least 1 hour, or until firm enough to handle.
Prepare a breading station: Place flour in one shallow dish, beaten eggs in a second, and panko breadcrumbs in a third.
Form potato mixture into cylindrical croquettes, about 6-7 cm long and 2-3 cm thick.
Dredge each croquette in flour, shaking off excess. Dip in beaten egg, ensuring full coverage. Roll in panko breadcrumbs, pressing gently to adhere.
Heat vegetable oil in a deep pot or fryer to 170°C.
Fry croquettes in batches for 3-4 minutes, or until golden brown and crispy. Ensure internal temperature is hot.
Remove with a slotted spoon. Drain on paper towels.
Serve hot, garnished with fresh chives.
notes: Chilling the potato mixture thoroughly is crucial for easier shaping and to prevent the croquettes from breaking apart during frying.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Tomato Mushroom Pasta
recipes.visual_description: Al dente tagliatelle pasta, coated in a rich, creamy, reddish-orange tomato sauce. Sautéed sliced cremini mushrooms, cooked to a golden-brown, are mixed throughout the pasta. Halved cherry tomatoes add bursts of bright red. A generous dusting of finely grated Parmesan cheese covers the top, melting slightly into the warm pasta. Fresh green basil leaves are scattered over the dish for a vibrant contrast. The pasta is served in a simple, deep, off-white ceramic bowl, placed on a well-used rustic wooden dining table. A standard metal fork rests casually beside the bowl. Natural, warm light highlights the comforting textures of the dish. Portions are modest and home-style.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread to sop up the sauce.
Offer extra grated Parmesan cheese at the table.
instructions: Cook pasta according to package directions until al dente. Reserve 120ml of pasta water before draining.
While pasta cooks, heat olive oil in a large pan over medium heat.
Add diced onion to the pan. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes. This is the base of your soffritto.
Add minced garlic to the pan. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add sliced mushrooms to the pan. Sauté until mushrooms are golden brown and have released their liquid, about 8-10 minutes.
Pour in crushed tomatoes. Bring to a gentle simmer. Cook for 10 minutes, stirring occasionally, to deepen flavors.
Stir in heavy cream and 50g of grated Parmesan cheese. Simmer for 2-3 minutes until sauce slightly thickens.
Add cooked pasta to the sauce. Toss to coat evenly. If needed, add reserved pasta water, 30ml at a time, to achieve desired consistency.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Serve immediately, garnished with remaining grated Parmesan and fresh torn basil.
notes: Adjust sauce consistency with reserved pasta water for a creamier or looser finish.
For a richer flavor, use a mix of mushroom varieties.

recipes.recipe_name: Sweet Wine Poached Apples and Strawberries with Candied Walnuts and Cinnamon Crème Fraîche
recipes.visual_description: The dessert is elegantly plated on a clean, round white porcelain dish. Pale golden apple wedges, cut into uniform segments, are artfully arranged, slightly overlapping. Vibrant ruby-red strawberry halves are nestled among the apples. A glistening, dark amber sweet wine reduction is generously drizzled over the fruit, catching the light. Beside the fruit, a refined dollop of creamy white cinnamon crème fraîche adds a soft contrast. Scattered around the fruit and crème fraîche are irregular chunks of amber-brown candied walnuts, providing textural interest. The overall presentation is balanced and uncluttered, with moderate negative space. The setting features a simple, light-colored wooden table surface. A silver dessert fork and spoon are placed to the right of the plate. A folded white cotton napkin rests beside the cutlery. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish, with a softly blurred, casual restaurant background.
instructions: Prepare poaching liquid: In a medium saucepan, combine sweet wine, water, 100g sugar, lemon juice, and cinnamon stick. Bring to a simmer over medium heat, stirring until sugar dissolves.

Poach apples: Add apple wedges to simmering liquid. Reduce heat to low. Simmer gently for 8-10 minutes, or until apples are tender-crisp. Do not overcook. Remove apples with a slotted spoon. Set aside.
Poach strawberries: Add strawberries to the same poaching liquid. Simmer for 1-2 minutes until slightly softened. Remove strawberries with a slotted spoon. Set aside.
Reduce poaching liquid: Increase heat to medium-high. Simmer remaining liquid rapidly until reduced to a thin syrup, about 8-12 minutes. Remove cinnamon stick. Set syrup aside to cool slightly.
Prepare cinnamon crème fraîche: In a small bowl, combine crème fraîche, 30g sugar, and vanilla extract. Whisk until smooth.

Assemble: Arrange poached apple wedges and strawberries on each of four dessert plates. Drizzle generously with the sweet wine syrup. Place a dollop of cinnamon crème fraîche beside the fruit. Scatter candied walnuts over and around the fruit. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Smoked Paprika Chicken with Braised Tomatoes and White Beans
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of Smoked Paprika Chicken is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. A creamy mound of golden-yellow smashed potatoes forms a bed. A succulent, whole braised chicken thigh, with its crispy, deep golden-brown skin, rests atop or beside the potatoes. A rich, reddish-brown sauce, studded with tender white cannellini beans and chunks of braised tomato, is spooned liberally over the chicken and potatoes, creating a vibrant, rustic appeal. The dish is garnished with a scattering of bright green, freshly chopped flat-leaf parsley, adding a pop of color and freshness. The textures are varied: the tender chicken, the creamy potatoes, and the slightly chunky sauce. The plate is positioned on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by standard flatware and a folded cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish, with a softly blurred, casual bistro background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread to soak up the rich sauce
Pair with a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and vinegar

ingredients.name: Canned cannellini beans, rinsed and drained

instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.

Heat olive oil in a large, oven-safe pan or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear chicken thighs skin-side down for 8-10 minutes until skin is deeply golden and crispy. Flip and sear for 2 minutes. Remove chicken from pan and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion to the pan. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until softened and translucent. Add minced garlic and smoked paprika. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in diced tomatoes, chicken broth, and rinsed cannellini beans. Bring the sauce to a gentle simmer. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pan.

Return seared chicken thighs to the pan, nestling them into the sauce. Cover the pan. Transfer to a preheated oven at 180°C (350°F). Braise for 25-30 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) and is very tender.
While chicken braises, peel and cut potatoes into large chunks. Place potatoes in a large pot. Cover with cold salted water. Bring to a boil. Cook for 15-20 minutes until very tender. Drain well.

Return drained potatoes to the hot pot. Mash them thoroughly with a fork or potato masher. Stir in a splash of olive oil or a knob of butter (optional) and season with salt and pepper to taste until creamy and smooth.

Remove chicken from oven. Ladle a generous portion of smashed potatoes onto each plate. Place one braised chicken thigh on top or beside the potatoes. Spoon the rich tomato and bean sauce generously over the chicken and potatoes.
Garnish with freshly chopped flat-leaf parsley before serving.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
Adjust smoked paprika to your preference for a milder or bolder flavor.

recipes.recipe_name: Clear Chicken Consommé with Fermented Rice & Seasonal Vegetables
recipes.visual_description: A single starter portion of Clear Chicken Consommé is presented in a shallow, wide-rimmed, handcrafted ceramic bowl with an organic, unglazed off-white finish. The consommé is perfectly clear and golden, reflecting natural light. At the bottom, a small, elegant scattering of distinct elements is visible: small diced white chicken pieces, individual grains of cooked white rice, and vibrant, precisely small-diced fermented vegetables—orange carrots and translucent daikon radish. A delicate cluster of fresh, bright green pea shoots rests gently on the surface, providing a natural, unfussy garnish. The composition is clean and minimalist, with ample negative space around the central dish. The bowl sits on a light-colored, reclaimed wood table surface, accompanied by an undyed linen napkin in a natural beige tone. Soft, diffused natural light illuminates the scene, highlighting the pure textures and colors of the ingredients. A subtle, out-of-focus green plant element is visible in the background, reinforcing the eco-conscious setting.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Roast chicken bones on a baking tray for 30 minutes until golden brown. This adds depth.
Transfer roasted bones to a large pot. Add roughly chopped onion, carrot, and celery. Add 1.5 L cold water.
Bring to a gentle simmer. Skim any foam. Reduce heat to low. Simmer for 2 hours. Do not boil vigorously.
Strain broth through a fine-mesh sieve lined with cheesecloth. Discard solids. Cool broth completely.
For clarification: In a bowl, whisk egg whites until frothy. Gently stir egg whites into the cooled broth.
Heat broth slowly over medium-low heat. Do not stir once it starts to form a 'raft' of egg whites. The raft traps impurities.
Simmer gently for 20-30 minutes, allowing the consommé to clarify. A small hole will form in the raft; ladle consommé through it.
Carefully ladle clear consommé through a fine-mesh sieve lined with fresh cheesecloth. Season consommé with salt and pepper. Keep warm.
Poach chicken breast in lightly salted water until internal temperature reaches 75°C. This takes about 10-12 minutes. Cool and then dice into small 5 mm cubes.
Finely dice fermented carrots and daikon radish into 3 mm cubes.
To serve: Ladle hot consommé into individual bowls. Add a small spoonful of cooked white rice. Add a few small diced chicken pieces. Add a small amount of diced fermented vegetables.
Garnish each bowl with a few fresh pea shoots or microgreens.
notes: This recipe utilizes chicken bones for a rich, flavorful broth, promoting zero-waste cooking.
Fermented vegetables introduce a tangy counterpoint and showcase sustainable preservation techniques.
The minimalist approach emphasizes the inherent beauty and flavor of each natural ingredient.

recipes.recipe_name: Crispy Chicken Cutlet with Cabbage Fritter and Strawberry BBQ Glaze
recipes.visual_description: A single, refined portion is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate, set on a simple light wooden table surface. The centerpiece is a golden-brown, crispy chicken cutlet, presented whole and unsliced. Beside it, a round, savory cabbage fritter with visible shreds of green cabbage, orange carrot, and white potato shows a delicate pan-fried crust. A vibrant, glossy reddish-brown strawberry BBQ glaze is artfully drizzled over the chicken and around the plate, creating appealing lines without overwhelming the dish. A bright yellow lemon wedge sits beside the chicken. A sprinkle of fresh green chopped parsley or chives adds a final touch of color and freshness. The scene is well-lit with natural, even lighting, and a folded cotton napkin rests beside the plate, all against a subtly blurred, casual restaurant background.
instructions: Prepare the Strawberry BBQ Glaze: Halve strawberries. Mince 1 garlic clove. Combine strawberries, ketchup, sugar, chili flakes, minced garlic, and juice from half lemon in a saucepan. Bring to a simmer over medium heat. Cook 10-12 minutes, stirring occasionally, until strawberries soften and sauce thickens. Remove from heat. Blend until smooth. Keep warm.

Prepare Cabbage Fritters: Shred cabbage, carrot, and potato. Finely dice remaining onion and 1 garlic clove. In a large bowl, whisk 1 egg with milk. Add shredded cabbage, carrot, potato, diced onion, diced garlic, and 50g flour. Mix well. Season with salt and pepper.

Heat 2 cm of vegetable oil in a large non-stick pan over medium-high heat. Drop spoonfuls of fritter mixture into hot oil to form 4 round fritters. Cook 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through. Drain on paper towels. Keep warm.

Prepare Chicken Cutlets: Pound each chicken breast to 1.5 cm thickness. Season both sides with salt and pepper. Set up a breading station: one plate with remaining flour, one shallow dish with remaining whisked egg, and one plate with panko breadcrumbs.
Dredge each chicken cutlet first in flour, shaking off excess. Dip in egg, letting excess drip off. Finally, coat generously in panko breadcrumbs, pressing gently to adhere.

Heat 2 cm fresh vegetable oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Add chicken cutlets, do not overcrowd. Fry 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown and internal temperature reaches 75°C. Drain on paper towels.

Plate immediately: Place one cabbage fritter on each plate. Place one crispy chicken cutlet next to the fritter. Drizzle generous amount of Strawberry BBQ Glaze over chicken and around the plate. Garnish with a fresh lemon wedge and finely chopped parsley or chives. Serve hot.

recipes.recipe_name: Roasted Carrot and Herb Rice Salad
recipes.visual_description: The Roasted Carrot and Herb Rice Salad is presented on a clean, white porcelain dinner plate, centrally placed on a simple light wooden table surface. The salad forms a vibrant, appealing mound, showcasing a harmonious blend of colors and textures. Fluffy white basmati rice forms the base, interspersed with golden-orange roasted carrot rounds, their edges slightly caramelized. Bright red halved cherry tomatoes and crisp green cucumber cubes add pops of color. Finely diced red onion and a hint of minced green chili are visible throughout, offering subtle contrast. Fresh green chopped parsley and mint are generously mixed in, providing verdant freshness and an aromatic garnish. The salad is lightly coated with a glistening lemon-herb vinaigrette, reflecting natural, even lighting. A cotton napkin is neatly folded beside the plate. The overall presentation is clean, professional, and inviting, with moderate negative space emphasizing the fresh ingredients.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm pita bread
Can be part of a mezze platter with hummus and olives
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Cut carrots into 1 cm thick rounds. Toss with 15 ml olive oil, salt, and pepper.
Spread carrots on a baking tray. Roast for 20-25 minutes until tender and slightly caramelized. Let cool.
Rinse rice thoroughly. Cook rice according to package directions. Fluff with a fork. Let cool completely.
While rice cools, prepare vegetables. Halve cherry tomatoes. Dice red onion finely. Mince green chili. Dice cucumber into 1 cm cubes.
For the dressing, whisk together remaining 65 ml olive oil, lemon juice, minced garlic, and ground cumin in a small bowl. Season with salt and pepper.
In a large bowl, combine cooled rice, roasted carrots, halved cherry tomatoes, diced red onion, minced green chili, diced cucumber, and drained chickpeas.
Add chopped parsley and mint. Pour dressing over salad.
Toss gently to combine all ingredients. Serve immediately or chill.

recipes.recipe_name: Spiced Chocolate Bean Cake with Dark Beer Glaze
recipes.visual_description: A single square slice of rich, dark chocolate bean cake rests centrally on a clean white porcelain plate. The cake has a deep, fudgy brown color and a slightly moist, dense texture. A glossy, dark amber dark beer glaze is generously drizzled over the top and cascades down the sides of the cake. Beside the cake, a vibrant, reddish-orange dollop of spiced tomato-lime compote offers a bright contrast. Scattered around and on top of the cake are small, irregular pieces of golden-brown, glistening beef and grains of paradise crumble, providing a crunchy texture. A delicate, pale golden Kefalotiri crisp stands upright, leaning against the cake, adding a refined, salty element. The plate is surrounded by moderate negative space on a simple wooden table surface, with a neatly folded cotton napkin beside it. Natural, even lighting highlights the textures and colors, creating a professional yet approachable presentation. The beef is presented as small, crisp crumbles, not sliced.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a small shot of Anejo Tequila or Mezcal on the side for an authentic after-dinner experience.
Pair with a rich, dark roasted coffee or a Mexican hot chocolate.

ingredients.name: Canned kidney beans, rinsed and drained
Beef sirloin or tenderloin, finely minced

instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C. Grease and flour an 20 cm square baking pan.

For the Beef & Grains of Paradise Crumble: Heat a small pan over medium heat. Add finely minced beef. Render fat and crisp beef until very dry and crumbly. Drain excess fat. Return beef to pan. Add 15g granulated sugar and 1.5g ground grains of paradise. Cook, stirring, until sugar melts and coats beef, forming a crisp, sweet crumble. Spread on parchment paper to cool. Break into small pieces.

For the Dark Beer Glaze: In a small saucepan, combine dark beer and 30g granulated sugar. Bring to a simmer over medium heat. Reduce until thickened to a syrupy consistency, about 10-15 minutes. Set aside.

For the Spiced Tomato-Lime Compote: In a small saucepan, combine diced tomatoes, 30g granulated sugar, lime juice, and a pinch of cayenne pepper (if using). Bring to a simmer. Cook, stirring occasionally, until tomatoes soften and mixture thickens to a jam-like consistency, about 10 minutes. Set aside.

For the Kefalotiri Crisps: Grate Kefalotiri cheese finely. Arrange small, thin mounds of grated cheese on a parchment-lined baking sheet. Bake for 5-7 minutes, or until golden brown and crispy. Let cool completely. Break into irregular shards.
For the Chocolate Bean Cake: In a food processor, blend rinsed kidney beans and 30 ml water until very smooth. Set aside.
In a large bowl, whisk together flour, cocoa powder, remaining 75g granulated sugar, brown sugar, baking powder, baking soda, salt, and remaining 1.5g ground grains of paradise.
In a separate bowl, whisk together eggs, melted butter, vanilla extract, and pureed kidney beans.
Pour wet ingredients into dry ingredients. Mix until just combined. Do not overmix.
Pour batter into the prepared baking pan. Bake for 25-30 minutes, or until a wooden skewer inserted into the center comes out with moist crumbs.
Let cake cool in pan for 10 minutes. Invert onto a wire rack to cool completely.

To serve: Cut cake into 4 equal portions. Place one slice on each serving plate. Drizzle generously with Dark Beer Glaze. Add a spoonful of Spiced Tomato-Lime Compote beside the cake. Sprinkle Beef & Grains of Paradise Crumble over the cake and plate. Garnish with a Kefalotiri Crisp standing upright.
notes: Ensure kidney beans are blended completely smooth for the best cake texture.
The beef crumble provides a surprising savory-sweet crunch; ensure it's very finely minced and well-crisped before candying.

recipes.recipe_name: Mediterranean Roasted Chicken with Herbed Rice, Roasted Carrots, and Olive-Tomato Salad
recipes.visual_description: A single roasted chicken thigh, golden-brown and tender, is presented atop a generous bed of fluffy herbed rice on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. Alongside, several vibrant orange roasted carrot chunks, slightly caramelized, are neatly arranged. A fresh, colorful salad of halved bright red cherry tomatoes, plump yellow corn kernels, and dark purple Kalamata olive halves provides a burst of color and texture. Freshly chopped green basil and oregano leaves are scattered throughout the salad and lightly over the chicken and rice, adding aromatic freshness. A delicate drizzle of extra virgin olive oil glistens over the entire dish. The plate sits on a simple wooden table, with a neatly folded cotton napkin placed beside it. The scene is illuminated by soft, natural, even lighting, creating a relaxed, modern bistro atmosphere. A small basket of crusty bread is subtly visible in the background, suggesting a complete meal. The overall presentation is professional yet inviting, with appropriate negative space highlighting the quality ingredients.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread for dipping in olive oil or juices.
Enjoy with a light dry white wine.
A simple green salad can accompany the main dish.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Prepare chicken: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season with 5g salt and 3g black pepper. Set aside.
Prepare carrots: Wash and peel carrots. Cut into 3cm chunks. In a bowl, toss carrot chunks with 15ml olive oil, 1 crushed garlic clove, 2g salt, and 1g black pepper.
Roast chicken and carrots: Arrange seasoned chicken thighs and carrot chunks in a single layer on a large baking tray. Roast for 30 minutes.
Check chicken temperature: Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C.

Prepare herbed rice: While chicken roasts, finely dice the small onion. In a medium saucepan, heat 15ml olive oil over medium heat. Add diced onion and remaining 2 crushed garlic cloves. Sauté until softened, about 3 minutes. Add rice and stir for 1 minute until lightly toasted. Pour in chicken broth. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 15-18 minutes, until liquid is absorbed and rice is tender. Fluff with a fork.

Prepare olive-tomato salad: While chicken, carrots, and rice cook, halve cherry tomatoes. Halve pitted Kalamata olives. Roughly chop fresh basil and oregano. In a medium bowl, combine halved tomatoes, halved olives, corn kernels, chopped basil, and chopped oregano.
Dress salad: Zest half the lemon into the salad. Squeeze juice from the whole lemon into the salad. Add 50ml olive oil, 2g salt, and 1g black pepper. Toss gently to combine.

Plate: Create a bed of herbed rice on each plate. Place one roasted chicken thigh on top of the rice. Arrange roasted carrot chunks alongside the chicken and rice. Spoon a generous portion of the olive-tomato salad next to the chicken and carrots.
Serve: Offer crusty bread on the side. Optionally, sprinkle crumbled feta cheese over the salad.
notes: Adjust seasoning to taste.
For crispier carrots, turn them halfway through roasting.
Ensure chicken is cooked through before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Cotoletta di Pollo alla Milanese con Patate e Carote Arrosto e Mostarda di Fragole
recipes.visual_description: A golden-brown Cotoletta di Pollo alla Milanese is the centerpiece on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The chicken cutlet, pounded thin and perfectly crispy, rests prominently. Beside it, a generous portion of roasted 2cm potato cubes and carrot chunks, tender with slightly caramelized edges, are neatly arranged. A small, vibrant dollop of ruby-red strawberry mostarda is placed near the chicken, offering a contrasting color. Fresh lemon wedges and a sprinkle of chopped fresh parsley adorn the plate. The composition is balanced and inviting, with moderate negative space. The setting is a modern bistro, featuring a simple wooden table surface. Standard European flatware is placed beside the plate, with a folded cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and rich colors, against a soft, casual restaurant background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with additional lemon wedges for squeezing over the chicken.
Offer a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and white wine vinegar.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Cut potatoes and carrots into 2cm cubes/chunks. Place on a baking tray. Add crushed garlic, rosemary, 30ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Toss to coat. Roast for 30-35 minutes, until tender and lightly browned. Turn once.

Prepare strawberry mostarda. Hull and quarter strawberries. Finely dice red onion. Combine strawberries, onion, sugar, white wine vinegar, water, and a pinch of salt in a small saucepan. Bring to a simmer over medium heat. Cook for 15-20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until thickened. Stir in dry mustard powder. Set aside.
Prepare chicken cutlets. Place each chicken breast between two sheets of parchment paper. Pound evenly to about 1cm thickness. Season both sides with salt and pepper.
Set up breading station. Place flour in a shallow dish. Whisk eggs in a second shallow dish. In a third dish, combine breadcrumbs, grated Parmesan, finely chopped parsley, and lemon zest.
Dredge each chicken cutlet in flour, shaking off excess. Dip in beaten egg, ensuring full coverage. Transfer to breadcrumb mixture. Press firmly to adhere breadcrumbs evenly on both sides.

Heat 100ml olive oil and butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Once butter is melted and oil shimmers, carefully add chicken cutlets. Do not overcrowd the pan; cook in batches if necessary.
Fry chicken for 4-5 minutes per side, until golden brown and cooked through. Internal temperature should reach 75°C (167°F). Transfer cooked cutlets to a wire rack to drain excess oil.
Serve chicken cutlets immediately with roasted potatoes and carrots. Garnish with fresh lemon wedges and a dollop of strawberry mostarda.

recipes.recipe_name: Rigatoni with Chicken and Sausage
recipes.visual_description: A single generous serving of Rigatoni with Chicken and Sausage is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate, centrally placed on a simple light wooden table. The rigatoni is coated in a rich, deep red tomato sauce, naturally piled without excessive arrangement. Diced chicken pieces, approximately 2.5 cm, are visibly browned and nestled among the pasta, alongside savory crumbled Italian sausage. The dish is vibrant with the red of the sauce, the golden-brown of the meats, and a scattering of fresh, bright green chopped parsley as garnish. A dusting of finely grated Parmesan cheese lightly covers the top. The overall presentation is professional yet approachable, with moderate negative space on the plate. Beside the plate, a neatly folded light grey cotton napkin and traditional Italian flatware (fork and spoon) are arranged. In the softly blurred background, a small white bowl holds extra grated Parmesan, and a few fresh thyme sprigs hint at the dish's aromatic profile. Natural, even lighting highlights the textures and colors, creating an inviting, casual bistro atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread to sop up the sauce
A simple green salad with vinaigrette
instructions: Dice chicken thighs into 2.5 cm pieces. Remove sausage from casings; crumble.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Add crumbled sausage. Cook, breaking up with a spoon, until browned. Remove sausage with a slotted spoon; set aside.
Add diced chicken to the same skillet. Cook until browned on all sides. Internal temperature should reach 75°C.
Remove chicken; set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion to the skillet. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and red pepper flakes (if using). Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in crushed tomatoes and chicken broth. Add thyme sprigs. Bring to a simmer.
Reduce heat to low. Simmer for 15 minutes, allowing flavors to meld.
Meanwhile, cook rigatoni according to package directions until al dente. Drain, reserving 125 ml pasta water.
Remove thyme sprigs from sauce. Return cooked sausage and chicken to the skillet. Stir to combine.
Add drained rigatoni to the sauce. Toss well to coat.
Stir in grated Parmesan cheese. If sauce is too thick, add reserved pasta water, a little at a time, until desired consistency.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Serve immediately, garnished with fresh chopped parsley and extra Parmesan.
