notes: Ensure chicken reaches 75°C internal temperature for safety.
Adjust spice level with red pepper flakes.

recipes.recipe_name: Crispy Chicken and Potato Croquettes with Tangy Slaw and Strawberry Ketchup
recipes.visual_description: Three golden-brown, cylindrical chicken and potato croquettes are centrally plated on a pristine white ceramic dish. Each croquette boasts a perfectly crisp, textured crust. Beside them, a vibrant mound of finely julienned carrot and shredded green cabbage slaw adds a fresh, crunchy contrast. A small, rich red pool of strawberry ketchup, smooth and glossy, is artfully placed to the side for dipping. A delicate sprig of fresh parsley or a thin lemon wedge garnishes the plate, enhancing color and flavor. The arrangement is clean and balanced, allowing moderate negative space. The dish sits on a light wooden table, suggesting a casual yet refined bistro setting, illuminated by soft, natural light.
instructions: Boil potatoes until tender. Drain. Mash thoroughly. Set aside.
Poach or bake chicken breast until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Shred or finely chop chicken. Set aside.
Mince garlic. Finely dice half the onion. In a pan, melt 20g butter. Sauté diced onion and minced garlic until softened. Remove from heat.
In a large bowl, combine mashed potatoes, shredded chicken, sautéed onion and garlic, milk, 30g butter, salt, and pepper. Mix well to form a cohesive mixture.
Shape mixture into 12-16 cylindrical or oval croquettes.
Prepare three shallow dishes: one with flour, one with beaten eggs, and one with breadcrumbs.
Dredge each croquette in flour, then dip in egg, then coat thoroughly in breadcrumbs. Press gently to ensure full coverage.
Heat vegetable oil in a deep pot or fryer to 175°C. Fry croquettes in batches for 4-6 minutes, or until golden brown and crispy. Ensure internal temperature is hot. Drain on paper towels.

For the strawberry ketchup: Hull and quarter strawberries. In a small saucepan, combine strawberries, sugar, ketchup, and juice of half a lemon. Simmer over medium-low heat for 10-15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until strawberries soften and sauce thickens. Mash or blend until smooth. Season with salt to taste.

For the slaw: Finely julienne carrots. Shred cabbage. In a bowl, combine carrots and cabbage. Whisk remaining lemon juice with 2 tablespoons of vegetable oil, salt, and pepper. Toss dressing with vegetables.
Serve hot croquettes with a side of fresh slaw and strawberry ketchup. Garnish with chopped fresh parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Pappardelle al Ragù Bolognese
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of Pappardelle al Ragù Bolognese is presented in a clean, white porcelain pasta bowl. A generous mound of broad, flat pappardelle noodles is loosely intertwined with a rich, thick, reddish-brown ragù. The mincemeat, finely diced carrots, celery, and onions are visibly integrated within the sauce, creating a textured, cohesive coating on the pasta. The dish is garnished with a scattering of freshly grated, pale yellow Parmigiano Reggiano and a few vibrant green, torn fresh basil leaves. The overall presentation is inviting, with a balanced composition and moderate negative space. The bowl sits on a simple wooden table, accompanied by a folded cotton napkin and classic silver flatware, under natural, even lighting in a modern bistro setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with extra grated Parmigiano Reggiano on the side.
Accompany with crusty Italian bread for dipping.
Pair with a robust red wine like Sangiovese or Chianti.
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium heat.
Add diced pancetta. Cook until crispy. Remove pancetta, set aside. Leave rendered fat in pot.
Add finely diced onion, carrot, and celery (soffritto) to the pot. Cook until softened, about 8-10 minutes. Do not brown.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Increase heat to medium-high. Add mincemeat to the pot. Break it apart with a spoon. Brown meat thoroughly on all sides. Drain excess fat if necessary.
Pour in red wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Simmer until wine has almost completely evaporated.
Add milk. Simmer until milk has almost completely evaporated and absorbed by the meat.
Stir in crushed tomatoes and tomato paste. Add beef stock. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Reduce heat to low. Cover partially. Simmer for at least 2-3 hours, stirring occasionally. The longer it simmers, the richer the flavor. Add a little hot water or stock if sauce becomes too thick.
Season the ragù with salt and black pepper to taste.
Just before serving, cook pappardelle pasta in a large pot of salted boiling water according to package instructions until al dente.
Drain pasta. Add pasta directly to the ragù in the pot. Toss to coat thoroughly.
Serve immediately. Garnish each portion with fresh basil leaves and grated Parmigiano Reggiano.
notes: Authentic Bolognese requires a long, slow simmer for the best flavor development.
Do not rush the evaporation steps for the wine and milk, as they contribute significantly to the ragù's depth.
The ragù should be thick enough to cling to the pasta, not watery.

recipes.recipe_name: Smoky Chipotle Pork Medallions with Black Bean Puree
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate, centrally composed with thoughtful negative space. Two to three thick-cut, pan-seared pork medallions, exhibiting a deep golden-brown crust with tender interiors, are nestled beside a generous quenelle of rich, dark black bean puree. The puree is smooth and creamy, its deep, almost black hue providing a striking contrast to the pork. A vibrant green sprig of fresh cilantro rests gracefully atop the pork, adding a pop of color and freshness. A bright lime wedge is placed on the side of the plate. The composition is clean and organized, yet feels organic and approachable. The lighting is natural and even, highlighting the textures and colors of the food. The setting is a modern bistro with a simple light wooden table surface and a folded cotton napkin beside the plate.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm corn tortillas for scooping the puree.
Offer a side of simple avocado slices or a fresh jicama salad.
instructions: Trim pork loin. Slice into 2.5 cm thick medallions. Season pork generously with salt and black pepper.

Heat 15ml olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Sear pork medallions 3-4 minutes per side until golden brown. Cook to an internal temperature of 63°C (145°F). Transfer pork to a plate. Tent with foil. Let rest 3 minutes.
Add remaining 15ml olive oil to the same pan. Add diced onion. Sauté 3 minutes until softened. Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in drained black beans, chopped chipotle chiles, adobo sauce, cayenne pepper, and chicken stock. Bring to a simmer. Cook 5 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Transfer bean mixture to a food processor or blender. Add hot sauce, lime juice, and chopped cilantro. Blend until smooth and creamy. Add a splash more stock if too thick. Season with salt to taste.
Spoon black bean puree onto serving plates. Arrange 2-3 pork medallions beside the puree. Garnish with fresh cilantro sprigs.

recipes.recipe_name: Classic Beef Ragu with Tagliatelle
recipes.visual_description: A generous serving of Classic Beef Ragu with Tagliatelle is presented in a deep, rustic ceramic bowl. The broad, golden tagliatelle ribbons are coated in a rich, dark red-brown beef ragu. The sauce features finely broken, tender beef mincemeat and soft, diced vegetables (onion, carrot, celery) from the long simmer. The pasta is al dente, naturally intertwined with the hearty sauce. A generous, uneven sprinkle of freshly grated Parmigiano Reggiano cheese tops the dish, some melting gently into the warm ragu. The overall plating is natural and abundant, filling the bowl without overcrowding. The bowl sits on a well-worn wooden dining table. Simple, everyday flatware and a casually folded linen napkin are placed alongside. Warm, inviting light illuminates the scene, evoking a comfortable, lived-in Italian family kitchen.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread for dipping
Offer extra grated Parmigiano Reggiano at the table
Pair with a simple, robust red wine
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium heat.
Add diced onion, carrot, and celery. Cook until softened, about 8-10 minutes. Do not brown.
Increase heat to medium-high. Add beef mincemeat. Break it apart with a spoon. Cook until browned, about 5-7 minutes. Drain excess fat.
Stir in tomato paste. Cook for 1 minute.
Pour in red wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Cook until wine evaporates, about 3 minutes.
Add crushed tomatoes and beef stock. Stir well.
Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for at least 1.5 hours, or up to 3 hours, stirring occasionally. The longer, the better.
Season ragu with salt and black pepper to taste.
Cook tagliatelle according to package instructions in salted boiling water until al dente.
Drain pasta. Add directly to the ragu pot. Toss to coat the pasta thoroughly with the sauce.
Serve immediately. Garnish with grated Parmigiano Reggiano.
notes: The ragu's flavor deepens significantly with longer simmering times.
This ragu freezes well for future meals.

recipes.recipe_name: Classic Beef Bolognese with Rigatoni
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Classic Beef Bolognese with Rigatoni is presented on a clean, white porcelain dinner plate, centrally placed on a simple wooden table. The rigatoni pasta is generously coated in a rich, deep red Bolognese sauce, with visible small, browned chunks of minced beef interspersed throughout. The sauce has a glossy, thick texture, clinging well to the ridged pasta. Fresh, vibrant green basil leaves are artfully scattered over the top, providing a striking color contrast. A generous dusting of finely grated white Parmesan cheese completes the dish. The plating is organized yet natural, allowing the sauce and pasta to appear inviting and abundant without overcrowding. The scene is bathed in soft, natural, even lighting, highlighting the food's colors and textures. Beside the plate, a neatly folded cotton napkin and traditional silver flatware are arranged. The background is minimal, suggesting a modern bistro setting with a casual atmosphere, keeping the focus entirely on the authentic Italian main course.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with extra grated Parmesan cheese on the side.
Offer crusty Italian bread for dipping in the sauce.
Pair with a glass of dry red wine.
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Add minced beef. Cook, breaking it up with a spoon, until browned. Drain excess fat. Remove beef from pot.
Add diced onion, carrot, and celery to the pot. Sauté for 8-10 minutes until softened, stirring occasionally. This is the soffritto.
Add minced garlic and tomato paste. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring constantly, until fragrant.
Pour in red wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Cook until wine mostly evaporates, about 3-4 minutes.
Return browned beef to the pot. Add crushed tomatoes and beef broth. Stir well.
Bring sauce to a simmer. Reduce heat to low. Cover and cook for at least 1.5 hours, or up to 3 hours, stirring occasionally. The longer it simmers, the richer the flavor.
Season sauce with salt and black pepper to taste.
About 15 minutes before serving, cook rigatoni according to package directions in salted boiling water until al dente.
Drain pasta. Add cooked pasta directly to the Bolognese sauce. Stir to combine thoroughly.
Serve hot, garnished with fresh basil leaves and grated Parmesan cheese.
notes: For a deeper flavor, simmer the Bolognese sauce for a longer duration, up to 3 hours, adding more broth or water if it becomes too thick.
Ensure the soffritto vegetables are properly softened before adding other ingredients to build a strong flavor base.

recipes.recipe_name: Classic Bolognese with Tagliatelle
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of Classic Bolognese with Tagliatelle is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The golden tagliatelle pasta is neatly coiled, forming a refined, natural mound. It is generously coated with a rich, deep red-brown Bolognese sauce, showcasing chunky pieces of slow-cooked beef and pork ragu. Scattered over the pasta are vibrant green fresh basil leaves and a light dusting of finely grated Parmigiano-Reggiano cheese. A few crispy diced pancetta pieces are visible. The dish has a balanced composition with moderate negative space. The setting features a simple light wooden table surface, with a silver fork and a folded white cotton napkin placed beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and colors against a soft, blurred restaurant-style background.
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large heavy-bottomed pot over medium heat.
Add diced pancetta. Cook until crispy. Remove pancetta, set aside. Leave rendered fat in pot.
Add ground beef and pork to the pot. Brown thoroughly, breaking up meat with a spoon. Drain excess fat.
Add diced onion, carrot, and celery (soffritto) to the pot. Cook until softened, about 8-10 minutes.
Stir in minced garlic and tomato paste. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Pour in red wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Cook until wine is mostly evaporated.
Stir in crushed tomatoes, beef broth, milk, salt, and pepper. Bring to a simmer.
Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for at least 2 hours, or up to 4 hours, stirring occasionally. The longer it simmers, the richer the flavor.
Cook tagliatelle according to package directions until al dente.
Drain pasta. Add pasta directly to the Bolognese sauce. Toss to coat well.
Stir in chopped fresh basil and most of the cooked pancetta.
Serve immediately. Garnish each portion with remaining crispy pancetta and freshly grated Parmigiano-Reggiano.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Tomato Orzo with Pickled Bell Peppers
recipes.visual_description: A small, elegant starter portion is presented centrally on a round, handcrafted ceramic plate in a natural cream tone, allowing ample negative space. The orzo, cooked to al dente, is folded into a rich, vibrant red-orange fermented-style tomato sauce, creating a cohesive yet textured base. Artfully arranged atop the orzo are thin, glossy batons of quick pickled red and yellow bell peppers, their bright colors providing crisp visual contrast and subtle tang. A delicate drizzle of single cream subtly swirls into the sauce. The dish is garnished with a few small, fresh basil leaves, their deep green providing a final natural touch. The setting features a light, textured reclaimed wood surface. A simple, undyed linen napkin is folded neatly. Soft, natural light illuminates the scene, highlighting textures and colors. The background is clean and minimalist, with a hint of natural greenery.
instructions: Prepare Quick Pickled Bell Peppers: In a small saucepan, combine 120 ml white wine vinegar, 120 ml water, 1 tbsp sugar, 1 tsp salt, 5 black peppercorns, and 1 bay leaf. Bring to a boil, stirring until sugar and salt dissolve. Remove from heat. Slice red and yellow bell peppers into thin batons. Add bell pepper batons to a heatproof jar. Pour hot pickling liquid over bell peppers, ensuring full submersion. Let cool to room temperature. Refrigerate for at least 30 minutes.

Prepare Fermented-Style Tomato Sauce: Heat 2 tbsp olive oil in a saucepan over medium heat. Add diced red onion and sauté until softened, about 5 minutes. Add minced garlic and cook for 1 minute until fragrant. Add chopped tomatoes, vegetable stock, 1 tbsp white wine vinegar, and 1/2 tsp sugar. Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to low, cover, and cook for 20-25 minutes, stirring occasionally, until tomatoes break down. Season with salt and pepper.

Cook Orzo: Bring a pot of salted water to a boil. Add orzo and cook according to package directions until al dente, typically 8-10 minutes. Drain well. Toss cooked orzo with 1 tbsp olive oil to prevent sticking.

Combine and Finish: Add the cooked orzo to the tomato sauce. Stir gently to combine. Gradually stir in the single cream until well incorporated and heated through. Taste and adjust seasoning if needed.

Plate and Serve: Divide the orzo mixture among four small starter plates or bowls. Arrange a few quick pickled bell pepper batons artfully on top of each serving. Garnish with fresh basil leaves or finely chopped chives. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Seared Egg and Grapefruit Salad with Chili-Coriander Dressing
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a clean, simple white porcelain dinner plate, set on a natural wooden table surface. Two seared eggs, with crisp, slightly frilly edges and vibrant runny yolks, are the central focus. They rest atop a bed of thinly sliced, bright green cucumber ribbons, artfully arranged to create a fresh base. Juicy, pink-hued grapefruit segments are neatly placed around the eggs, adding bursts of color and citrusy appeal. A generous drizzle of the emerald green chili-coriander dressing glistens over the components. The salad is garnished with fresh, verdant coriander leaves and a few thin, bright red slices of green chili for a touch of heat and visual contrast. The plating is clean and balanced, with moderate negative space. A cotton napkin and simple chopsticks are placed beside the plate, hinting at a modern Asian bistro setting with natural, even lighting.
instructions: Segment grapefruits. Remove all white pith and membranes. Set aside.
Thinly slice cucumber into ribbons using a mandoline or vegetable peeler. Set aside.
For the dressing, finely chop one green chili and half of the fresh coriander. Mince garlic cloves.
In a small bowl, whisk together lime juice, fish sauce, sugar, minced garlic, chopped green chili, and chopped coriander. Add sesame oil. Stir well. Taste and adjust seasoning.
Heat vegetable oil in a large non-stick skillet over medium-high heat.
Carefully crack eggs into the hot skillet. Cook 2-3 minutes until whites are set and edges are crispy. Yolks should remain runny. Cook in batches if necessary. Season with salt and pepper.
Arrange cucumber ribbons artfully on individual serving plates. Place grapefruit segments around the cucumber.
Carefully transfer two seared eggs onto each plate, resting them on the cucumber and grapefruit.
Drizzle generously with the chili-coriander dressing.
Garnish with remaining fresh coriander leaves and thin slices of the second green chili.

recipes.recipe_name: Butter Chicken
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of vibrant Butter Chicken is presented in a clean, shallow white porcelain bowl. Generous 3-4cm chunks of seared, tender chicken are nestled in a rich, creamy, and smooth orange-red tomato-yogurt gravy. The sauce shimmers with a glossy finish. A delicate swirl of fresh white cream adorns the surface, contrasting beautifully with the sauce's deep hue. The dish is garnished generously with bright green, freshly chopped coriander leaves, adding a pop of color and freshness. The chicken pieces maintain their shape, not sliced. The bowl is placed on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by a small, separate bowl of fluffy white basmati rice and a piece of soft, torn naan bread. A clean, folded cotton napkin rests nearby. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's inviting colors and textures, set against a subtly blurred, casual restaurant background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve hot with fluffy Basmati rice.
Accompany with fresh naan bread or roti for scooping the gravy.
Offer a side of cooling raita (yogurt dip) or sliced red onion.

ingredients.name: Cashews
ingredients.quantity: 30g, soaked in hot water for 15 minutes

instructions: Combine chicken chunks with yogurt, 20g ginger-garlic paste, 2g turmeric powder, 5g Kashmiri red chili powder, and a pinch of salt. Mix well. Marinate for at least 30 minutes in the refrigerator.
Melt 30g ghee or butter in a large pot or deep pan over medium heat. Add chopped onion. Sauté until translucent, about 8-10 minutes.

Add remaining 20g ginger-garlic paste. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant. Add 3g turmeric powder, 5g Kashmiri red chili powder, cumin powder, and coriander powder. Sauté for 30 seconds until aromatic, adding a splash of water if spices stick.
Add crushed tomatoes and soaked cashews to the pot. Bring to a simmer. Cook for 10-15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the sauce thickens slightly.

Remove the pot from heat. Allow to cool slightly. Carefully transfer the sauce mixture to a blender. Blend until completely smooth. Strain through a fine-mesh sieve back into the pot for a silkier texture, if desired.

In a separate pan, sear the marinated chicken chunks in a small amount of oil or ghee over medium-high heat until lightly browned on all sides. Do not overcrowd the pan; cook in batches if necessary. Chicken does not need to be cooked through at this stage.

Add the seared chicken chunks to the smooth tomato gravy in the pot. Add 150ml water or chicken stock. Bring to a gentle simmer. Cover and cook for 15-20 minutes, or until chicken is tender and cooked through (internal temperature 75°C).

Crush kasoori methi between your palms and add to the pot. Stir in garam masala. Add the remaining 30g unsalted butter and heavy cream. Stir until butter melts and cream is incorporated. Do not boil after adding cream.
Taste and adjust salt as needed. Garnish with fresh coriander leaves before serving.
notes: For best flavor, marinate the chicken overnight.
Adjust the amount of Kashmiri red chili powder to control the spice level; it primarily provides color.
The gravy can be made ahead of time and stored in the refrigerator for up to 3 days.

recipes.recipe_name: Seared Tuna Loin, Roasted Bell Pepper Essence, Tagliolini, Lemon Cream
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of an ultra-sophisticated dish is presented on a large, pristine white bone china plate. A shallow, vibrant pool of clear, red-orange roasted bell pepper essence forms the base, occupying the plate's center. Off-center, a delicate, artfully arranged nest of golden tagliolini sits elegantly. Resting against the pasta is a thick, perfectly seared tuna loin, exhibiting a deep, crisp crust and a striking pink interior. A light, ethereal cloud of bright white lemon cream foam is carefully placed beside the tuna. A few tiny, bright green micro basil leaves are precisely scattered to add a final touch of color and freshness. The plate rests on a luxurious white Carrara marble surface. A crisp white linen napkin, folded into a precise triangle, is positioned beside the plate. Dramatic, focused lighting casts soft shadows, enhancing the dish's contours and textures. The background is clean and minimalist, allowing the dish to be the sole focal point.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a crisp, light-bodied Italian white wine such as Vermentino or Pinot Grigio.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Halve bell peppers, remove seeds. Place cut-side down on baking sheet. Roast 20-25 minutes until skin blisters. Transfer to bowl, cover tightly. Let steam 10 minutes. Peel and discard skins. Roughly chop roasted bell peppers.

Finely dice shallot and garlic. In a saucepan, heat a small amount of olive oil. Sauté shallot and garlic until fragrant, about 2 minutes. Add chopped tomatoes and roasted bell pepper. Cook 5 minutes.

Deglaze with white wine. Reduce by half. Add vegetable stock. Simmer 15 minutes. Remove from heat. Carefully blend mixture until very smooth. Strain through a fine-mesh sieve or cheesecloth, pressing solids to extract all liquid. Discard solids. Season essence with sea salt and black pepper. Keep warm.

In a small saucepan, gently warm heavy cream. Stir in lemon zest and a squeeze of lemon juice. Season with a pinch of sea salt. Using an immersion blender or whisk, aerate the cream until a light foam forms. Keep warm and foamy.

Bring a large pot of salted water to a rolling boil. Add tagliolini. Cook according to package directions until al dente. Drain pasta immediately. Toss with a drizzle of olive oil to prevent sticking.

Pat tuna loins dry. Season generously with sea salt and black pepper on all sides. Heat a heavy-bottomed pan or cast iron skillet over high heat until smoking. Add a thin film of olive oil. Carefully place tuna loins in the hot pan. Sear 1-2 minutes per side for rare to medium-rare. Adjust time for desired doneness. Remove tuna from pan. Rest 2 minutes.

To plate, spoon a shallow pool of the warm bell pepper essence onto the center of each large, individual plate. Create a small, artful nest of tagliolini slightly off-center in the essence. Place one seared tuna loin against the pasta. Gently spoon a dollop of lemon cream foam next to the tuna. Garnish with a few micro basil leaves. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Mediterranean Pan-Seared Chicken with Lemon-Herb Sauce
recipes.visual_description: A single, golden-brown pan-seared chicken thigh, skin-on and whole, is centrally placed on a clean white porcelain plate. It's surrounded by halved bright red cherry tomatoes and dark Kalamata olives. A rich, amber pan sauce, infused with herbs, pools around the chicken and vegetables. Fresh green oregano and parsley are scattered for contrast. The chicken skin exhibits a beautiful, crispy sear. A small portion of fluffy orzo pasta accompanies the dish. The setting is a simple wooden table with natural lighting, a folded cotton napkin, and standard flatware, reflecting a professional bistro aesthetic.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread to dip in the sauce
Accompany with a simple green salad with lemon vinaigrette
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs skin-side down for 8-10 minutes until golden brown and crispy.
Flip chicken. Cook for 2-3 minutes on the other side. Remove chicken from skillet.
Reduce heat to medium. Add sliced shallots to the skillet. Sauté for 3 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in white wine. Deglaze the pan, scraping up any browned bits. Simmer for 2 minutes.
Add chicken stock, cherry tomatoes, and Kalamata olives to the skillet. Bring to a simmer.
Return chicken thighs to the skillet, skin-side up.
Transfer skillet to a preheated oven at 180°C (350°F). Bake for 15-20 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C.
Remove skillet from oven. Stir in fresh oregano, parsley, and lemon juice.
Check seasoning. Serve immediately.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
Bone-in, skin-on chicken thighs provide best flavor and moisture.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Garlic Herb Beef and Chicken with Mushroom Cream Sauce
recipes.visual_description: Plated on a clean white porcelain dinner plate, a single serving features two pan-seared beef medallions and one golden-brown chicken breast piece. The beef, with a rich brown crust, is nestled beside the chicken. A generous ladle of creamy, light brown mushroom sauce, with visible sliced mushrooms and herb flecks, coats the meats. Fresh green chopped parsley is scattered over the top, providing vibrant contrast. The arrangement is organic, balanced, with moderate negative space. Textures include seared meat, tender mushrooms, and a smooth, rich sauce. The plate rests on a simple wooden table with silver flatware and a folded cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish. The background is minimal, suggesting a casual bistro setting.
instructions: Pat beef and chicken dry. Season generously with salt and pepper. Cut beef into 8 medallions. Cut chicken breast into 4 pieces or thick slices.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear beef medallions for 2-3 minutes per side for medium-rare. Remove from skillet. Set aside.
Add chicken pieces to the same skillet. Sear for 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through (internal temperature 75°C). Remove and set aside with beef.
Add butter to the skillet. Sauté diced shallot until softened, about 2 minutes.
Add sliced mushrooms. Cook until browned and tender, about 5-7 minutes.
Stir in minced garlic, chopped rosemary, and thyme. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in chicken broth. Bring to a simmer, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the skillet. Reduce heat to medium.
Stir in heavy cream. Simmer gently for 5 minutes, or until sauce slightly thickens. Season with salt and pepper.
Return beef and chicken to the skillet. Spoon sauce over the meats. Heat gently for 1-2 minutes.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Mediterranean Orzo with Roasted Vegetables and Farmer Cheese
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Mediterranean Orzo with Roasted Vegetables and Farmer Cheese is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. The orzo forms a golden base, loosely piled but with structure. Vibrant red and yellow roasted bell pepper strips are interspersed throughout, along with deep green broccoli rabe florets. Creamy white crumbled farmer cheese is visible, some pieces slightly melted into the warm orzo, others retaining their shape. Julienne strips of rich red sun-dried tomatoes add concentrated color. The dish is garnished with a scattering of fresh green oregano leaves. Textures are a mix of al dente pasta, tender-crisp vegetables, and soft, creamy cheese. The plate is positioned on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by standard silver flatware and a folded cotton napkin beside it. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's fresh colors and textures. The background is minimally blurred, suggesting a casual bistro atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm, crusty bread for dipping
Pair with a simple green salad dressed with lemon vinaigrette
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Slice red and yellow bell peppers into thick strips. Toss with 15 ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Roast on a baking sheet for 20 minutes, or until tender and slightly charred. Set aside.

Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Add broccoli rabe florets and stems. Blanch for 2 minutes. Drain immediately and plunge into ice water to stop cooking. Drain well and chop roughly. Set aside.
Cook orzo pasta according to package directions until al dente. Drain, reserving 100 ml pasta water. Set aside.
While pasta cooks, heat remaining 45 ml olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add minced garlic and red pepper flakes if using. Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant. Do not brown.
Add chopped sun-dried tomatoes and chopped blanched broccoli rabe to the skillet. Sauté for 3-4 minutes. Stir in roasted bell pepper strips.
Add cooked orzo to the skillet. Pour in vegetable broth and reserved pasta water. Stir well. Cook for 2 minutes until liquid is slightly reduced.
Remove skillet from heat. Crumble farmer cheese directly into the pasta. Add chopped fresh oregano. Stir gently until cheese is just melted and creamy. Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Serve immediately. Garnish with additional fresh oregano or grated Parmesan cheese if desired.
notes: Use high-quality olive oil for best flavor.
Adjust red pepper flakes to desired spice level.

recipes.recipe_name: Sous Vide Chicken Breast, Truffled Potato Puree, Black Garlic Jus
recipes.visual_description: A minimalist, elegant plating on a pristine white bone china plate. A generous, organic swirl of velvety truffled potato puree forms the base, its creamy ivory color contrasting subtly with the plate. Beside it, two or three thick, golden-crusted pan-seared chicken breast medallions, their interiors moist and white, are arranged naturally, not fanned. A rich, glossy, dark mahogany black garlic jus is artfully spooned around the chicken and puree, creating fluid lines. The dish is accented by a single, delicate sprig of vibrant green microgreens or a precisely cut chive baton, providing a pop of fresh color. The composition emphasizes abundant negative space, showcasing precise cooking and luxurious textures. The plate rests on a polished dark wood surface, illuminated by dramatic, directional light casting soft shadows, with a crisp white linen napkin folded precisely nearby.

ingredients.name: Unsalted butter, cold, cut into cubes

instructions: Season chicken breasts with salt and pepper. Place each breast in a vacuum-sealable bag with one thyme sprig and 10ml olive oil. Vacuum seal.
Cook chicken in a sous vide water bath at 63°C for 1.5 hours.
Peel and dice potatoes into 2cm cubes. Place in a saucepan, cover with cold salted water. Bring to a boil, reduce heat, and simmer until very tender (about 15-20 minutes). Drain well.

Pass hot potatoes through a fine-mesh sieve or potato ricer into a clean saucepan. Add heavy cream and 70g cold butter cubes. Whisk vigorously until smooth and creamy. Stir in truffle oil. Season with salt to taste. Keep warm.
Peel black garlic cloves. In a small saucepan, combine black garlic and chicken stock. Bring to a simmer. Cook gently for 10 minutes to infuse.
Transfer the black garlic mixture to a high-speed blender. Blend until completely smooth. Pass through a fine-mesh sieve into a clean saucepan.

Return jus to low heat. Whisk in remaining 30g cold butter cubes until emulsified and glossy. Season with salt and pepper. If desired, whisk in a tiny pinch of xanthan gum for slight thickening. Keep warm.

Once sous vide cooking is complete, remove chicken from bags. Pat dry thoroughly with paper towels. Heat 30g butter in a heavy-bottomed skillet over medium-high heat until shimmering. Sear chicken breasts for 2-3 minutes until deeply golden brown and crisp. Flip and sear other side for 1-2 minutes. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C. Rest chicken for 5 minutes.

Slice each chicken breast into 2-3 thick, diagonal medallions (not fanned). Spoon a generous dollop of truffled potato puree slightly off-center on each plate. Arrange chicken pieces naturally beside the puree. Spoon black garlic jus artfully around the chicken and puree. Garnish with microgreens or chive batons.

recipes.recipe_name: Stuffed Plantain with Savory Beef and Burdock
recipes.visual_description: A single, perfectly roasted ripe plantain rests diagonally on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The plantain is split lengthwise, revealing a generous, richly colored savory filling of finely diced burdock root, browned ground beef, and vibrant red bell pepper. The burdock is tender, contrasting with the soft, caramelized plantain. A sprinkle of bright green chopped fresh cilantro garnishes the filling, adding a pop of color and freshness. A neat lime wedge sits beside the plantain, ready to be squeezed. The plate features moderate negative space, highlighting the dish as the focal point. The scene is set on a simple wooden table, with a neatly folded cotton napkin beside the plate. Natural, even light illuminates the dish, emphasizing its inviting textures and warm, earthy tones. The presentation is professional, approachable, and visually balanced.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Peel plantains. Slice each plantain lengthwise, not all the way through, creating a pocket.
Place plantains on a baking sheet. Drizzle with 15 ml olive oil. Bake 20-25 minutes, until tender and slightly golden.
While plantains bake, heat remaining 15 ml olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add ground beef. Cook until browned, breaking it apart. Drain excess fat.
Add diced onion, red bell pepper, and finely diced burdock to the skillet. Sauté 5-7 minutes, until vegetables soften.
Stir in minced garlic, tomato paste, cumin, smoked paprika, and oregano. Cook 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Pour in beef broth. Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to medium-low. Cook 10-12 minutes, until liquid reduces and flavors meld. Season with salt and pepper.
Remove plantains from oven. Carefully open each plantain pocket.
Spoon generous amount of beef and burdock filling into each plantain.
Garnish with chopped fresh cilantro. Serve immediately with lime wedges.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Fermented Garlic & Seasonal Greens
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a minimalist, matte white ceramic plate, showcasing a single, generous individual portion. Pan-seared chicken thighs, cooked to a golden-brown exterior, are cut into thick, rustic chunks and arranged centrally. The chicken is moist and tender, revealing its natural texture. Alongside, a vibrant bed of deep green, wilted seasonal leafy greens, such as Swiss chard or kale, is artfully mounded, its stalks visible and tender. The greens are glossy from the pan drippings and subtly flecked with the creamy, beige fermented garlic paste. Bright orange carrot rounds and delicate purple-red slices of quick-pickled red onion are scattered sparingly around the plate, providing sharp color contrast and a crisp texture. The overall composition is clean and organic, with ample white space on the plate. The setting features a light, textured wooden surface, an undyed linen napkin in a natural beige, and soft, diffused natural lighting. The focus remains entirely on the wholesome, natural beauty of the ingredients, presented simply and elegantly.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve alongside a simple grain like quinoa or brown rice, or with crusty sourdough bread to soak up the juices.

ingredients.name: Seasonal leafy greens (e.g., kale, Swiss chard), stems included
Large carrot, thinly sliced into rounds
Salt and freshly ground black pepper
Lemon, half juiced, half thinly sliced for garnish

instructions: Prepare quick pickled vegetables: Thinly slice carrot and red onion. In a small saucepan, combine apple cider vinegar, 120ml water, 15g sugar, and 5g sea salt. Bring to a simmer, stirring until sugar and salt dissolve. Pour hot brine over sliced vegetables in a heatproof jar. Set aside to cool.

Prepare fermented garlic paste: Peel 2 heads of garlic. Blend cloves with 20g sea salt and 100ml water until a smooth paste forms. Transfer to a clean jar, seal loosely, and ferment at room temperature for 1-2 weeks until bubbly and tangy.

Cook chicken: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and black pepper. Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Sear chicken thighs for 5-7 minutes per side until golden brown. Cook until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken from skillet. Let rest on a cutting board for 5 minutes.

Sauté greens: While chicken rests, add leafy greens (stems first, then leaves) to the same skillet with residual oil. Sauté for 3-5 minutes until wilted and tender. Stir in 15-20g of the prepared fermented garlic paste. Squeeze in juice from half a lemon. Season with a pinch of salt if needed.

Assemble dish: Slice rested chicken thighs into thick chunks. Arrange sautéed greens on individual plates. Top with chicken chunks. Drain quick pickled vegetables and scatter over the chicken and greens. Garnish with a thin lemon slice if desired.
notes: The fermented garlic paste is a key flavor component and requires preparation 1-2 weeks in advance. If time is limited, substitute with roasted garlic cloves mashed into a paste or very finely minced fresh garlic sautéed until deeply golden and soft.
This recipe embraces a zero-waste philosophy by utilizing entire parts of vegetables, like leafy green stems, and preserving ingredients through fermentation and quick pickling.

recipes.recipe_name: Pollo Rustico con Risotto al Parmigiano e Uovo Fritto
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. A generous portion of creamy, free-flowing Parmigiano Risotto forms the base, its pale yellow hue contrasting with the golden-brown, crispy-skinned roasted chicken thigh, positioned slightly off-center. Alongside, a single fried egg, with its crisp edges and visible, vibrant yellow yolk, rests against the chicken or on the risotto. Rustic chunks of roasted potato, with their browned exteriors, are scattered around the plate, adding earthy tones. The dish is garnished simply with freshly chopped green parsley and a light dusting of grated Parmigiano Reggiano, enhancing its inviting aroma and color balance. The overall presentation is organized yet organic, allowing for moderate negative space. The table setting includes a simple cotton napkin and basic flatware, with natural, even lighting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a glass of dry white wine such as Pinot Grigio or Vermentino.
Offer crusty ciabatta bread on the side for soaking up the rich risotto.

ingredients.name: Small potatoes, cut into 2-3 cm chunks

instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Pat chicken thighs dry. Season with salt, pepper, rosemary, and thyme. Toss potato chunks with olive oil, salt, and pepper.
Place chicken and potatoes on a baking tray. Roast for 30-40 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C and skin is crispy. Potatoes should be tender and browned.
While chicken roasts, prepare breadcrumbs. Process stale bread into coarse crumbs.
For the risotto, heat 30ml olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add diced onion; cook until translucent, about 5 minutes (Soffritto). Add minced garlic; cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Add Arborio rice to the pot. Toast rice for 2 minutes, stirring constantly. Pour in white wine; stir until absorbed.

Begin adding hot chicken stock, one ladle at a time. Stir continuously. Wait for each ladleful to be absorbed before adding the next. This process takes about 18-20 minutes. Risotto should be creamy and al dente.
Remove risotto from heat. Stir in 40g butter and 80g Parmigiano Reggiano (Mantecatura). Season with salt and pepper. Stir in half of the chopped parsley.

Heat remaining 30ml olive oil in a non-stick pan over medium-high heat. Coat eggs in breadcrumbs. Fry eggs one at a time until edges are crispy and yolk is still runny, about 2-3 minutes per side. Remove and drain on paper towel.

Plate immediately. Serve a portion of risotto on a plate. Top with a roasted chicken thigh and fried egg. Arrange roasted potato chunks around the plate. Garnish with remaining fresh parsley and a sprinkle of Parmigiano Reggiano.

recipes.recipe_name: Perkedel Jagung Kari Merah dengan Acar Fermentasi
recipes.visual_description: Golden-brown, rustic corn fritters are arranged casually on a light, textured reclaimed wood board. Each fritter is roughly circular, about 6-7 cm in diameter, with visible whole corn kernels embedded in a subtly red-orange matrix. The edges are slightly irregular and crisp. Adjacent to the fritters, a small, handcrafted ceramic bowl in an earthy cream tone holds a vibrant quick-fermented acar. The acar features thinly sliced cucumber, carrot, and shallots, with a few small red chili slices, glistening with pickling liquid. A few fresh cilantro sprigs are scattered over the fritters and near the acar, adding a pop of green. The overall plating is natural and unforced, with ample negative space. The background is minimalist, with a hint of natural light and an undyed linen napkin in beige. The entire arrangement is presented as a relaxed sharing portion, highlighting the natural textures and colors of the ingredients. The fritters are whole pieces, not cut or fanned.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve as a light snack or appetizer.
Often enjoyed with a cup of hot tea or coffee.
Can be accompanied by a simple sambal for extra heat.

ingredients.name: Indonesian Red Curry Paste (Bumbu Kari Merah)

instructions: Prepare Acar: Thinly slice cucumber, carrot, and shallots. Combine vinegar, sugar, water, and sliced chilies in a small bowl. Stir until sugar dissolves. Add sliced vegetables. Let sit for at least 30 minutes, or longer for more fermentation.

Prepare Curry Paste: If making from scratch, blend 5 red chilies, 3 shallots, 2 cloves garlic, 1 cm galangal, 1 stalk lemongrass (white part), 1 cm kencur, 1/2 tsp turmeric, 2 candlenuts, 1/2 tsp shrimp paste (optional), 1/2 tsp palm sugar, and 1/4 tsp salt into a smooth paste. Set aside 30 g.
Combine Fritter Batter: In a large bowl, whisk eggs. Stir in coconut cream and kewra water. Add cornmeal, salt, and white pepper. Mix well.
Add Corn and Curry Paste: Stir in fresh corn kernels and Indonesian Red Curry Paste into the batter. Mix until well combined.
Heat Oil: Heat vegetable oil in a large frying pan over medium heat. Oil should be about 2 cm deep.
Fry Fritters: Spoon about 2 tablespoons of batter per fritter into the hot oil. Flatten slightly. Do not overcrowd the pan.
Cook Fritters: Fry for 3-4 minutes per side, until golden brown and cooked through. Ensure corn is tender. Adjust heat as needed to prevent burning.
Drain Fritters: Transfer cooked fritters to a wire rack lined with paper towels to drain excess oil.
Serve: Arrange fritters on a serving platter. Serve immediately with the prepared acar on the side. Garnish with fresh cilantro.
notes: This recipe adapts the 'Panang curry paste' ingredient into an Indonesian 'Bumbu Kari Merah' for cultural authenticity, while incorporating the unique aromatic note of kewra water subtly into the fritter batter.
The acar (pickles) provide a fermented, refreshing counterpoint, utilizing zero-waste principles by using common vegetable scraps for pickling.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken and Squid Saffron Rice
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of Chicken and Squid Saffron Rice rests on a rustic, off-white ceramic plate. The rice is a warm, golden-yellow from saffron, studded with vibrant red diced bell pepper, green peas, and flecks of fresh green parsley. Browned chicken chunks, approximately 3 cm, are scattered throughout, alongside glistening white squid rings and whole tentacles, which show slight char from cooking. The dish has a slightly moist, cohesive texture, with some rice grains visibly separate. It is presented casually, as if scooped from a larger communal pan, with components naturally overlapping. The plate is placed on a well-used wooden dining table. A simple cloth napkin is casually folded beside the plate. A few lemon wedges are placed on the side. The lighting is warm and inviting, typical of a home kitchen. The entire plate is visible, with adequate negative space around the food.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with fresh lemon wedges for squeezing over the rice.
Offer crusty bread to soak up any remaining juices.
Traditionally eaten directly from the paella pan at the table in a communal setting before individual plating.
instructions: Cut chicken thighs into 3 cm chunks. Cut squid tubes into 1.5 cm rings. Leave tentacles whole.
Heat olive oil in a large, shallow pan over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken chunks until golden brown on all sides. Remove chicken from pan.
Add diced onion and red bell pepper to the pan. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Stir in minced garlic and smoked paprika. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add diced tomatoes to the pan. Cook for 3 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Return chicken to the pan. Add rice and stir to coat.
Warm chicken broth. Steep saffron threads in a small amount of warm broth for 5 minutes. Add saffron-infused broth and remaining broth to the pan.
Bring to a simmer. Spread rice evenly. Do not stir after this point.
Reduce heat to medium-low. Cook uncovered for 15-20 minutes, or until most liquid is absorbed and rice is almost tender. Add squid rings and tentacles during the last 5-7 minutes of cooking.
Stir in frozen peas. Cover the pan with a lid or foil. Let rest off heat for 5-10 minutes.
Check chicken internal temperature to ensure it reaches 75°C.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley and lemon wedges.

recipes.recipe_name: Spiced Brown Sugar Sable Entremet with Caramelized Onion Confit and White Cheddar Mousse
recipes.visual_description: A single, impeccably cut slice of entremet is presented on a pristine white porcelain plate with a subtle gold rim. The slice stands elegantly, revealing distinct, architectural layers. At the base is a crisp, light brown spiced brown sugar sable, providing a firm foundation. Above it, a golden-amber layer of glistening caramelized onion and lemon confit creates a vibrant visual contrast. The thickest layer is an airy, off-white white cheddar mousse, its creamy texture evident. The entire entremet is enveloped in a glossy, reflective lemon-brown sugar mirror glaze, catching the light with a soft sheen. A single, delicate curl of candied lemon peel is precisely placed atop the glaze, adding a bright yellow accent and textural interest. The plate is largely empty, emphasizing abundant negative space, highlighting the dessert as a sculptural centerpiece. The setting is a pristine white marble display surface, with dramatic professional lighting casting soft shadows to enhance depth and form. A precisely folded white linen napkin sits beside the plate, completing the ultra-minimalist, sophisticated haute patisserie presentation.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve alongside a small, delicate glass of traditional Moroccan mint tea.

ingredients.name: Mild white cheddar cheese, finely grated

instructions: Prepare the Brown Sugar Sable:
Combine flour, brown sugar, cinnamon, and ginger in a food processor. Pulse briefly.
Add cold diced butter. Pulse until mixture resembles coarse crumbs.
Add egg yolk. Pulse until dough just comes together.
Form dough into a disk. Wrap in plastic. Chill 30 minutes.
Roll dough 3 mm thick. Cut four 8 cm diameter rounds. Place on parchment-lined baking sheet.
Bake at 170°C for 12-15 minutes until golden. Cool completely.
Prepare the Caramelized Onion & Lemon Confit:
Thinly slice the yellow onion into half-moons.
Melt 15 g butter in a saucepan over medium-low heat. Add sliced onion. Cook slowly for 20-25 minutes until deeply caramelized and very soft, stirring occasionally.
Add 50 g brown sugar, 15 ml lemon juice, lemon zest, 30 ml water, and optional orange blossom water. Cook for 5-7 minutes, stirring, until liquid reduces to a syrupy consistency.
Cool completely. Divide into four portions.
Prepare the White Cheddar Mousse:
Bloom 5 g gelatin in 25 ml cold water. Set aside.
In a saucepan, gently heat 100 ml heavy cream and 50 ml whole milk. Do not boil.
Remove from heat. Add grated cheddar cheese. Stir until cheese melts completely. Strain through a fine-mesh sieve to remove any solids. Return liquid to clean saucepan.
Add softened cream cheese to the warm cheddar-milk mixture. Whisk until smooth.
Gently heat the bloomed gelatin until dissolved. Stir into the cheese mixture.
Add powdered sugar and vanilla extract. Stir well. Let cool to room temperature.
Whip 200 ml cold heavy cream to soft peaks.
Gently fold whipped cream into the cooled cheese mixture until combined. Be careful not to deflate.
Assembly:
Line four 8 cm diameter individual entremet rings or molds with acetate strips.
Place one sable round at the bottom of each mold.
Spoon a layer of caramelized onion confit over the sable (approx. 20 g per mold). Spread evenly.
Pour the white cheddar mousse over the confit, filling each mold. Smooth the tops.
Freeze for at least 4 hours, preferably overnight, until completely solid.
Prepare the Lemon Brown Sugar Mirror Glaze:
Bloom 5 g gelatin in 25 ml cold water. Set aside.
In a saucepan, combine 75 ml water, 100 g brown sugar, and glucose syrup. Bring to a boil, stirring until sugar dissolves. Remove from heat.
Add condensed milk and chopped white chocolate. Stir until chocolate is melted and smooth.
Gently heat the bloomed gelatin until dissolved. Stir into the glaze mixture.
Add 10 ml fresh lemon juice and optional yellow food coloring. Stir well.
Use an immersion blender to emulsify the glaze. Blend slowly to avoid air bubbles. Strain through a fine-mesh sieve.
Let glaze cool to 35-38°C for optimal pouring consistency.
Glaze and Garnish:
Remove frozen entremets from molds. Place on a wire rack over a baking sheet.
Pour the warm glaze evenly over each frozen entremet, ensuring full coverage. Let excess drip off.
Carefully transfer glazed entremets to serving plates using a thin spatula.
For candied lemon peel: Thinly slice lemon into rounds. Cook in simple syrup (1:1 sugar:water) until translucent. Dry on parchment paper. Cut into delicate curls.
Garnish each entremet with a delicate candied lemon peel curl.
notes: Use a very mild, high-quality white cheddar to ensure a subtle, balanced flavor that complements the sweetness, rather than overpowering it.
The caramelized onion confit is key to transforming the onion into a sweet, jam-like component.

recipes.recipe_name: Cuban Chicken and Rice with Black Beans
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a clean, white porcelain dinner plate, showcasing a generous portion of vibrant Cuban Chicken and Rice. Tender, succulent chicken chunks, cooked until golden and then simmered to perfection, are interspersed throughout the rich, saffron-infused yellow rice. The rice grains are separate and fluffy, absorbing the savory flavors of tomato, cumin, and bell pepper. Dark, glossy black beans are gently folded into the rice, adding a contrasting color and creamy texture. The overall composition is organic and inviting, with a scattering of fresh, bright green cilantro leaves providing a pop of color and freshness. The plate is moderately spaced, allowing the dish to breathe without being sparse or overcrowded. The background features a simple wooden table surface, a neatly folded cotton napkin, and a minimalist bistro setting, with natural, even lighting highlighting the dish's warmth and texture.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of fried plantains (maduros).
Offer hot sauce or mojo sauce on the side.
Serve with a simple green salad dressed with lime and olive oil.

ingredients.name: Canned black beans, drained and rinsed

instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large, heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs until golden brown on both sides. Remove chicken from pot. Set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion and bell pepper to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 5-7 minutes.
Add minced garlic, cumin, and oregano. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in tomato paste. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Deglaze the pot with white wine (or chicken broth), scraping up any browned bits. Cook until liquid reduces slightly.
Return chicken thighs to the pot. Add chicken broth, saffron (if using), and bay leaf. Bring to a simmer.
Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 20 minutes, or until chicken is nearly cooked through (internal temperature 70°C/158°F).
Remove chicken from pot. Shred or cut into large chunks. Set aside.
Add rinsed rice to the simmering broth in the pot. Stir well. Bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low, cover, and cook for 15-18 minutes, or until rice is tender and liquid is absorbed. Do not lift lid during cooking.
Gently stir in shredded chicken and drained black beans into the rice.
Cover and let rest off heat for 5 minutes.
Fluff with a fork. Check chicken internal temperature (75°C/167°F). Adjust seasoning as needed.
Garnish with fresh cilantro before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Tuscan Garlic Chicken with Mushrooms and Basil
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Tuscan Garlic Chicken is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. Two golden-brown, seared chicken breast medallions, each about 2cm thick, are positioned slightly overlapping towards the center. Around the chicken, a rustic yet organized arrangement of sautéed quartered cremini mushrooms and vibrant halved cherry tomatoes creates a rich, earthy base. Thinly sliced garlic bits and chopped sun-dried tomatoes are interspersed throughout the glossy, light amber sauce, which lightly coats the ingredients. A generous scattering of fresh, roughly torn basil leaves adds pops of bright green, contrasting with the deep reds and browns of the dish. The overall presentation is natural and abundant, with moderate negative space. The plate rests on a simple light wooden table. Standard silver flatware is placed to the side, with a folded white cotton napkin. Natural, soft, even lighting illuminates the dish from above, creating subtle shadows and highlighting the textures. The background is softly blurred, suggesting a casual bistro setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread to sop up the flavorful sauce.

ingredients.name: Boneless, skinless chicken breasts
ingredients.quantity: 4 (approx. 180-200g each), halved horizontally or cut into thick medallions

instructions: Pat chicken breasts dry. Season with salt and pepper. Dredge lightly in flour, shaking off excess.

Heat 30ml olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Sear chicken until golden brown and cooked through, about 4-5 minutes per side. Internal temperature must reach 75°C. Remove chicken from skillet. Set aside.
Add remaining 30ml olive oil to the skillet. Add quartered mushrooms. Sauté until tender and browned, about 5-7 minutes.
Add sliced garlic and chopped sun-dried tomatoes to the skillet. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in white wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pan. Reduce by half, about 2 minutes.
Stir in chicken broth and halved cherry tomatoes. Bring to a simmer.
Return chicken to the skillet. Simmer for 5-7 minutes, allowing chicken to absorb flavors and sauce to thicken slightly.
Remove from heat. Stir in unsalted butter until melted and incorporated.
Stir in fresh basil. Taste and adjust seasoning.
Serve immediately.
notes: This dish pairs well with a side of pasta or roasted potatoes.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Orange Glaze
recipes.visual_description: A single, pan-seared chicken breast, cooked to a rich golden-brown, is the centerpiece on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The chicken, presented as a whole piece, is generously coated with a glossy, amber-hued orange glaze that shimmers under the light. Fresh, vibrant orange segments are thoughtfully arranged alongside the chicken, providing a burst of bright color. A sprinkle of finely chopped fresh green parsley or chives adds a delicate contrast and freshness. The plate rests on a simple, light-toned wooden table surface. A neatly folded light grey cotton napkin is placed to the left of the plate. The background suggests a modern bistro, softly blurred to keep focus on the dish. Natural, even overhead lighting highlights the dish's textures and colors, creating an inviting, professional presentation.
instructions: Pat chicken breasts dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken breasts for 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown.
Transfer skillet to a preheated oven at 180°C (350°F). Bake for 10-15 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken. Rest on a cutting board.
While chicken rests, drain excess fat from skillet, leaving 15ml. Add shallots to skillet. Sauté 2-3 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic and thyme sprigs. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Deglaze with orange juice (from 2 oranges, about 150ml). Scrape up browned bits.
Add chicken stock. Bring to a simmer. Reduce by half, about 5-7 minutes.
Whisk in butter until sauce is glossy. Season with salt and pepper. For a thicker sauce, mix cornstarch with 15ml cold water, whisk into sauce, then simmer 1 minute.
Cut remaining orange into segments for garnish. Zest some orange peel into the sauce.
Plate chicken as a whole piece. Spoon orange glaze over chicken.
Garnish with fresh orange segments and chopped parsley or chives.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches 75°C internal temperature for food safety.
Rest chicken for at least 5 minutes after cooking to ensure it remains juicy.

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Apple and Lentil Stew
recipes.visual_description: A comforting, single portion of Hearty Apple and Lentil Stew fills a rustic, deep ceramic bowl. The stew presents a rich, earthy reddish-brown hue, with visible, tender chunks of bright orange diced carrots, pale green diced celery, and soft, lighter-colored diced apples. The red lentils are fully cooked, creating a thick, hearty, yet still fluid consistency. A sprinkle of vibrant green chopped fresh parsley rests on top, adding a fresh contrast. The bowl sits on a well-worn, natural wooden dining table, suggesting a homely kitchen setting. A simple, everyday fork is casually placed beside the bowl. Warm, diffused lighting illuminates the scene, enhancing the natural colors and inviting texture of the stew. The entire bowl is visible, with ample negative space around it, emphasizing its comforting simplicity.
instructions: Rinse red lentils under cold water. Drain.
Heat olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium heat.
Add diced onion, carrots, and celery. Sauté 5-7 minutes until softened.
Stir in minced garlic and dried thyme. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Add rinsed lentils, vegetable broth, and canned diced tomatoes to the pot. Add bay leaf.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer 15 minutes.
Stir in diced apples. Continue to simmer, uncovered, for another 10-15 minutes, or until lentils are tender and stew has thickened slightly.
Remove bay leaf. Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Ladle hot stew into bowls. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken Parmesan with Spaghetti
recipes.visual_description: A single, golden-brown chicken cutlet, generously topped with melted, bubbly mozzarella and Parmesan cheese, rests on a bed of perfectly cooked spaghetti. A rich, vibrant red marinara sauce pools around the chicken and coats the pasta. The chicken cutlet is a thick, substantial piece, not sliced. Fresh green basil leaves are scattered over the dish for a pop of color and freshness. The dish is presented on a simple, slightly off-white ceramic plate with natural imperfections, placed on a well-used wooden dining table. A basic silver fork lies beside the plate. The scene is illuminated by warm, cozy light, typical of a family kitchen, creating a lived-in, comforting atmosphere. The portion is modest and homely, filling the plate adequately without overcrowding.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a simple green salad dressed with vinaigrette.
Offer crusty bread for dipping in the extra sauce.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Prepare chicken: Place each chicken breast between two sheets of plastic wrap. Pound to 1.5 cm thickness using a mallet or rolling pin.
Set up breading station: Place flour in a shallow dish. Whisk eggs in a second shallow dish. Combine breadcrumbs, garlic powder, oregano, salt, and pepper in a third shallow dish.
Dredge each chicken cutlet in flour, shaking off excess. Dip in egg, coating completely. Press into breadcrumb mixture, ensuring full coverage.
Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear breaded chicken for 3-4 minutes per side until golden brown. Do not fully cook through. Transfer chicken to a plate.
Pour half of the marinara sauce into the skillet. Arrange seared chicken cutlets over the sauce.
Top each chicken cutlet with remaining marinara sauce. Sprinkle generously with mozzarella cheese, then Parmesan cheese.
Bake for 15-20 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C and cheese is bubbly and golden.
While chicken bakes, cook spaghetti according to package directions in salted boiling water until al dente. Drain well.
Serve baked chicken parmesan over a bed of spaghetti. Garnish with fresh basil leaves.
notes: Pounding the chicken ensures even cooking and tenderness.
Using an oven-safe skillet reduces cleanup.

recipes.recipe_name: Apple and Onion Risotto with Toasted Pecans
recipes.visual_description: A creamy, free-flowing Apple and Onion Risotto is presented centrally on a round, matte white porcelain plate. The risotto has a soft, pale golden hue, studded with small, tender cubes of caramelized apple and translucent slivers of onion. Its texture appears luscious and yielding, not stiff or dry. A scattering of roughly chopped, golden-brown toasted pecans provides a contrasting crunch and warmth across the surface. Several fresh green thyme sprigs are artfully placed, adding a pop of vibrant color and aromatic appeal. The plate features moderate negative space, allowing the risotto to be the clear focal point. It sits on a simple wooden table, accompanied by a folded cotton napkin and standard modern flatware. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's comforting warmth and inviting textures.
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large heavy-bottomed pot over medium heat.
Add thinly sliced onion. Sauté 5-7 minutes until translucent and soft.
Peel, core, and dice apples into 1 cm cubes. Add to pot. Cook 3 minutes until slightly softened.
Stir in Arborio rice. Cook 2 minutes, stirring constantly, until rice edges are translucent.
Pour in white wine. Stir until completely absorbed by the rice.
Add hot vegetable broth, one ladle (about 120 ml) at a time. Stir constantly.
Wait until liquid is almost fully absorbed before adding the next ladle of broth.
Continue adding broth and stirring for 18-20 minutes until rice is creamy and al dente.
Remove pot from heat. Stir in butter and grated Parmesan cheese.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste. Stir until smooth and creamy.
While risotto cooks, toast pecans in a dry pan over medium heat for 3-5 minutes until fragrant. Roughly chop.
Serve risotto immediately. Garnish each portion with toasted pecans and a fresh thyme sprig.

recipes.recipe_name: Mediterranean Herb Chicken and Beef Skewers
recipes.visual_description: The dish features two perfectly grilled skewers, one predominantly chicken and the other beef, artfully arranged on a clean, round white porcelain plate. The chicken pieces are golden-brown with visible grill marks, showcasing a tender, cooked interior. The beef cubes are seared to a rich brown, revealing a juicy, medium-rare center. Both meats are cut into uniform 2.5 cm cubes. Interspersed between the meat on the skewers are vibrant roasted bell pepper chunks (red, yellow, orange) and red onion wedges, displaying caramelized edges and a soft texture. A generous bed of roasted vegetables, including bell pepper chunks, red onion pieces, and burst cherry tomatoes, forms the base, exhibiting a medley of warm, earthy colors. The entire composition is garnished with fresh green oregano and thyme sprigs, and bright lemon wedges are placed beside the skewers, adding a pop of color and freshness. The plate is presented on a simple wooden table, accompanied by a folded white cotton napkin and standard silver flatware. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and vibrant colors. The presentation is clean, professional, and balanced, allowing moderate negative space to emphasize the quality ingredients.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of tzatziki or a fresh cucumber-yogurt sauce.
Offer warm pita bread or flatbread for dipping.
Accompany with a simple Greek salad.
instructions: Cut chicken breast into 2.5 cm cubes.
Cut beef sirloin into 2.5 cm cubes.
In a large bowl, combine chicken and beef cubes.
Mince garlic. Finely chop oregano, thyme, and rosemary.
Add minced garlic, chopped herbs, 30ml olive oil, juice of half lemon, 5g salt, and 3g black pepper to the meat. Mix well.
Marinate meat for at least 30 minutes at room temperature, or up to 4 hours refrigerated.
Preheat oven to 200°C (400°F).
Core and deseed bell peppers. Cut into 2.5 cm pieces.
Cut red onion into 2.5 cm pieces. Separate layers.
In a separate bowl, toss bell peppers, red onion, and cherry tomatoes with remaining 30ml olive oil, 5g salt, and 2g black pepper.
Spread vegetables on a baking sheet. Roast for 20-25 minutes, until tender and slightly charred.
Thread marinated chicken and beef cubes alternately onto skewers. Add bell pepper and onion pieces between meat. Aim for 4 chicken-dominant skewers and 4 beef-dominant skewers, or mix evenly.
Heat a grill pan or outdoor grill to medium-high heat.
Grill skewers for 8-10 minutes, turning frequently, until chicken is cooked through and beef reaches desired doneness. Chicken internal temperature must reach 75°C (167°F).
Let skewers rest for 5 minutes before serving.
notes: For food safety, ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).
Soak wooden skewers in water for 30 minutes before use to prevent burning.
traditional_techniques: Marinating meats for flavor and tenderness.

recipes.recipe_name: Spiced Squash Bread Pudding with Candied Chickpeas and Umami Glaze
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of warm Spiced Squash Bread Pudding is presented on a clean, round white porcelain plate, centrally placed. The pudding is a substantial square cut from the pan, golden-brown on top with visible caramelized edges and soft, creamy interior. Small specks of orange from the grated carrot are subtly visible within the pudding. A generous scattering of glossy, amber-colored candied chickpeas rests beside and on top of the pudding, offering a contrasting crisp texture. A rich, amber-hued umami glaze is artfully drizzled over the pudding and around the plate, creating subtle pools. The setting is a modern bistro, featuring a light wooden table surface and a folded grey cotton napkin beside the plate. Natural, soft, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its comforting textures and warm colors. The background is softly blurred, suggesting a casual restaurant atmosphere.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Toss squash chunks with a drizzle of olive oil. Roast for 25-30 minutes until tender and caramelized. Mash or blend until smooth.
In a large bowl, whisk eggs, 150g sugar, vanilla, cinnamon, nutmeg, and salt. Gradually whisk in milk and cream. Stir in mashed squash puree and grated carrot.
Place bread cubes in a 20x20cm baking dish. Pour custard mixture over bread. Press gently to submerge bread. Let sit for 30 minutes to absorb.
Preheat oven to 175°C. Bake bread pudding for 40-50 minutes, or until set and golden brown. A knife inserted near the center should come out clean.

While pudding bakes, heat 50g sugar with 30ml water in a small saucepan. Bring to a simmer. Add chickpeas. Cook, stirring constantly, until water evaporates and sugar crystallizes around chickpeas. Continue cooking over low heat, stirring, until sugar caramelizes lightly and chickpeas are crisp. Spread on parchment paper to cool.

In a small saucepan, combine chicken broth and maple syrup. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low. Simmer gently for 20-25 minutes, or until liquid reduces by half and becomes a syrupy glaze. Strain for smoothness.
Spoon warm bread pudding onto individual plates. Garnish with candied chickpeas. Drizzle generously with the umami glaze.

recipes.recipe_name: Classic Pasta Carbonara
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of Classic Pasta Carbonara is presented in a clean, shallow white porcelain bowl, centered on a simple light wooden table. The spaghetti is artfully piled and twirled into a natural mound, coated in a rich, creamy, golden-yellow sauce. Interspersed throughout the pasta are crispy, golden-brown cubes of rendered guanciale. A generous dusting of finely grated white Pecorino Romano cheese covers the top, contrasting with abundant coarse black pepper flecks. The sauce has a glossy, emulsified texture, clinging beautifully to each strand of pasta. The overall composition is balanced with moderate negative space, highlighting the dish's inviting warmth and rustic elegance. A silver fork is positioned to the side, ready for serving. Natural, even light illuminates the dish from above, emphasizing the textures and colors.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately after preparation.
Offer extra grated Pecorino Romano and black pepper at the table.
Accompany with a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and vinegar.

ingredients.name: Guanciale (or pancetta)
ingredients.quantity: 150 g, cut into 1 cm cubes or strips

instructions: Bring a large pot of salted water to a rolling boil. Add spaghetti. Cook according to package directions until al dente. Reserve 250 ml of pasta cooking water before draining.
While pasta cooks, heat a large non-stick pan over medium-low heat. Add guanciale. Render slowly until crispy and golden, about 8-10 minutes. Remove pan from heat. Do not discard rendered fat.
In a medium bowl, whisk together egg yolks, whole egg, grated Pecorino Romano, and black pepper until smooth and creamy.
Drain pasta. Immediately add hot spaghetti to the pan with rendered guanciale and fat. Toss to coat.

Quickly pour the egg mixture over the pasta, tossing vigorously with tongs. Add reserved pasta water, 30 ml at a time, continuously tossing until a creamy, emulsified sauce forms and coats the pasta. The heat from the pasta will cook the egg mixture without scrambling it.
Serve immediately.
notes: The key to Carbonara is the emulsification of egg, cheese, and pasta water to create a creamy sauce without cream.
Do not cook the egg mixture directly on heat, as it will scramble. The heat from the pasta is sufficient.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken and Tomato Risotto
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of creamy Chicken and Tomato Risotto is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. The risotto is free-flowing and spread naturally. Its vibrant orange-red hue contrasts with golden-brown seared chicken chunks, interspersed throughout. Halved, bright red cherry tomatoes add bursts of color and texture. Freshly grated Parmesan cheese lightly dusts the top, providing a pale yellow accent. A few fresh basil leaves are scattered as garnish, offering a pop of green. The plate sits on a simple light wooden table. A folded cotton napkin and traditional Italian flatware are placed beside it. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish from the side, enhancing its inviting appearance.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and balsamic vinegar.
Offer crusty ciabatta bread for dipping.

ingredients.name: Parmesan cheese
ingredients.quantity: 100 g, freshly grated, plus extra for serving

ingredients.name: Fresh basil
ingredients.quantity: 15 g, chopped, plus sprigs for garnish

instructions: Heat 15 ml olive oil in a large, heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Add chicken cubes. Sear until golden brown on all sides. Cook chicken to an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken from pot. Set aside.
Add remaining 15 ml olive oil to the pot. Add diced onion. Sauté until translucent, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add Arborio rice. Stir constantly for 2 minutes until grains are translucent at the edges.
Pour in white wine. Stir until completely absorbed.
Add a ladleful of hot chicken broth. Stir continuously until broth is absorbed.
Continue adding broth one ladleful at a time. Stir constantly. Wait for each addition to be absorbed before adding the next. This process takes about 18-20 minutes.
After 10 minutes, add halved cherry tomatoes to the risotto. Continue cooking and stirring.
When rice is al dente (creamy but with a slight bite), remove from heat.
Stir in cooked chicken, grated Parmesan cheese, and butter. Stir vigorously for 1 minute for mantecatura (creamy finish).
Stir in chopped fresh basil.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste. Serve immediately.
notes: Risotto requires constant stirring for optimal creaminess.
Ensure broth is hot for continuous cooking.

recipes.recipe_name: Arroz con Pollo Mexicano
recipes.visual_description: The Arroz con Pollo is presented on a pristine white ceramic dinner plate. Two golden-brown, skin-on chicken thighs, cooked whole, are prominently positioned atop a generous bed of vibrant, moist orange-red long-grain rice. The rice is studded with finely diced white onion, red bell pepper, and specks of green jalapeño, offering a rich tapestry of color and texture. Fresh, bright green chopped cilantro is sprinkled generously over the chicken and rice. A quartered lime wedge rests beside the chicken. The plate maintains moderate negative space. The setting includes a simple wooden table, a folded white cotton napkin, and a small ceramic bowl of vibrant salsa roja. A stack of warm corn tortillas in a woven basket completes the authentic Mexican dining experience under natural, even lighting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm corn tortillas.
Offer a side of salsa roja or pico de gallo.
Accompany with refried beans or a simple green salad.
Serve with a Mexican agua fresca.
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.

Heat oil in a large, heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear chicken skin-side down until golden brown and crispy, about 5-7 minutes. Flip and sear other side for 3-5 minutes. Remove chicken. Set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion, minced garlic, minced jalapeño, and diced bell pepper to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 5-7 minutes.
Add rice to the pot. Stir constantly for 2-3 minutes until lightly toasted.
Stir in ground cumin and dried oregano for 1 minute. Pour in crushed tomatoes and chicken broth. Scrape bottom of pot to loosen any browned bits. Bring to a simmer. Season with salt and pepper.
Return seared chicken thighs to the pot, nestling them into the rice mixture. Ensure chicken is partially submerged.
Cover the pot tightly. Reduce heat to low. Simmer for 20-25 minutes, or until rice is tender and liquid is absorbed. Chicken should reach an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).
Remove from heat. Let rest, covered, for 10 minutes before serving.
Garnish with fresh chopped cilantro and serve with lime wedges.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken and Mushroom Risotto
recipes.visual_description: Serve the risotto on a flat white porcelain dinner plate. The consistency is fluid and spreads naturally across the plate, appearing free-flowing rather than molded. The rice grains are distinct, coated in a glossy, creamy sauce. Large 3cm chunks of golden-brown seared chicken thighs are distributed throughout the rice. Sliced cremini and shiitake mushrooms show deep caramelization and earthy brown tones. The dish features a pale golden hue. Finely minced flat-leaf parsley provides a vibrant green contrast. A light dusting of finely grated Parmesan cheese covers the surface. The arrangement is organic. Beside the plate sits a heavy silver spoon and a folded white cotton napkin on a light oak table. Natural side lighting highlights the creamy texture.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately while the consistency remains fluid
Accompany with a crisp dry white wine such as Pinot Grigio
Provide extra grated Parmesan at the table
instructions: Cut chicken thighs into 3cm chunks.
Dice onion into 5mm pieces.
Mince garlic cloves.
Slice mushrooms into 5mm thick pieces.
Heat 20ml olive oil in a wide pan over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken chunks until browned and internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Remove chicken from pan and set aside.
Add mushrooms to the same pan. Sauté until moisture evaporates and edges brown.
Remove mushrooms and set aside.
Melt 20g butter in the pan. Add onion and garlic.
Cook until softened but not browned.
